name: _shard_notes
justification: Screenshot review: the Read tool returned empty results for every PNG and JPEG in this run, so visual scores are based on code plus pixel statistics computed from the certification PNGs. 15 of the 17 captures have a white corner background (255), a mean luminance around 243-247, and a standard deviation of 8-15. That means a near-white page with faint, low-contrast grey content; there is no rich material, depth, or colour. The exceptions are the gallery, image viewer, and lazy image, which show photo content. All 17 targets are marked 'passed' with empty issuesFound in reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification.json, despite the functional defects listed above, so that certification is not evidence of quality. GlassFilterBar has no certification target.

name: _screenshot_review_note
justification: Methodology note, not a component. Visual scores above rest mainly on code-level rendering analysis plus the pixel statistics.

name: _internals_note
justification: Informational record only. Visual-quality note for the whole shard: the Read tool returned empty content for every certification PNG (and for JPEG conversions), so the PNGs could not be viewed. Visual scores are based on code plus certification DOM metrics (glassElementCount, hasCanvas) from reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification.json. All 17 entries are marked 'passed' with zero issues, even though three render only an empty fallback and EnhancementShowcase is invisible under reduced motion; this shows the certification does not test behaviour.

name: GlassAppShell (app-shell subpath)
target: single canonical AppShell (merge with src/components/layout/GlassAppShell.tsx) built on real CSS (a CSS module or shipped stylesheet) with responsive sidebar collapse
justification: The slot API is the right shape for a first-party app frame, and a premium shell is a natural flagship. The implementation is a class-string sketch, though. Its grid templates, min-height and surface background point to utility classes the library never ships, because there is no Tailwind compile and glass.css does not define them. Two exported components share the name GlassAppShell, and neither has an honest story. The app-shell has to own its CSS, merge with the root layout version and gain responsive behaviour before it can be a flagship.

name: GlassIconButton (app-shell, non-shim internal export)
target: GlassButton icon size
justification: It duplicates GlassButton's icon mode, has no story or docs, and does not have a shim file of its own.

name: GlassActionBar
target: GlassToolbar
justification: This is a styled div that duplicates GlassToolbar. It lacks toolbar semantics, and its radius is undefined.

name: GlassBreadcrumbs
target: src/components/navigation/GlassBreadcrumb.tsx
justification: Its semantics are correct, but it is visually generic and duplicates the root GlassBreadcrumb. It cannot render router links. Keep the a11y pattern and merge it into a single breadcrumb.

name: GlassCommandDock
target: GlassCommandPalette inline mode
justification: This is a decorative wrapper whose accent border and radius never render. GlassCommandPalette already covers the command UI.

name: GlassMain
target: AppShell.Main slot of canonical shell
justification: This is a trivial landmark wrapper. Applying blur across the whole page is the wrong default for a scroll container, and it is incompatible with the library's own skip-link target. Keep it only as a slot of the canonical shell.

name: GlassMobileShell
target: responsive canonical AppShell
justification: A separate mobile shell signals that the main shell is not responsive. This one has no safe-area handling, its grid classes are undefined and it nests main landmarks. Make the main shell responsive instead.

name: GlassPage
target: GlassContainer
justification: It duplicates GlassContainer, and its only feature (the max-width constraint) has no CSS behind it.

name: GlassPageHeader
target: single PageHeader (merge with layout/GlassAppShell PageHeader) with headingLevel and responsive action wrap
justification: The component is useful and simple, but it duplicates PageHeader in the root layout. It forces an h1, does not wrap its actions on mobile, and its eyebrow uses an undefined, hard-coded sky colour.

name: GlassResizablePanel
target: real resizable panel primitive (or the root GlassSplitPane)
justification: The name promises resizing that does not exist, its default maxSize is invalid CSS, and it has no story or test. Shipping it misleads users.

name: GlassSidebarPanel
target: GlassSidebar
justification: This is a thin aside wrapper. Its width is undefined, collapsing it leaves keyboard focus inside hidden content, and it has no story. Merge it into the canonical sidebar.

name: GlassSidebarRail
target: GlassSidebar (collapsed/rail mode) using GlassRovingFocusGroup + link polymorphism
justification: The library already has three sidebar implementations, and this one is the thinnest. Its active and focus states depend on undefined classes, so it is visually flat. It has no roving focus and cannot act as a router link. Fold it into GlassSidebar as a rail mode with real active-state material and keyboard behaviour.

name: GlassSplitPane (app-shell subpath)
target: src/components/layout/GlassSplitPane.tsx
justification: It shares its name with the root export, but most of its ratios are no-ops and it has no splitter. It adds confusion and gives users nothing beyond a CSS grid. Remove it and re-export the root SplitPane from the app-shell subpath.

name: GlassStatusBar
target: AppShell.StatusBar slot (live region opt-in)
justification: This is a thin footer whose always-on live region announces every update. Keep it as a shell slot and make announcements opt-in.

name: GlassTopBar
target: canonical AppShell.TopBar (consolidate GlassHeader/GlassToolbar)
justification: The API is minimal and sensible. It misses the premium bar because sticky positioning, corner radius, height and border do not resolve to any CSS. It also hand-rolls a white-alpha surface instead of using the library's material system, and it overlaps three other header/toolbar components. Rebuild it as part of a single shell with real material tokens.

name: AccessibilityProvider
target: single preferences provider merged with ReducedMotionProvider and the theme provider; settings must map to real CSS/token switches
justification: A real a11y preferences layer would make the library stand out. This one stores flags that nothing consumes, does not detect OS preferences automatically, and its wrapper div's overflow-x:hidden breaks sticky positioning, which matters for the app-shell. It is one of four competing settings models. Redesign it as the single source that drives data-attributes the token CSS actually responds to.

name: ContrastGuard
target: token-level contrast contract (pre-computed text-on-material pairs per theme) + useLiquidGlassBackdrop sampling where real; drop runtime guard
justification: The component claims WCAG enforcement but computes against white for any CSS-variable or hex text colour, assumes success on its fallback path, and writes CSS variables nothing reads. It leaks a MutationObserver on every unmount. Runtime contrast guessing is the wrong approach for a premium system. Guarantee contrast at token level, and use the existing LiquidGlassMaterial backdrop sampling where adaptive behaviour is genuinely needed.

name: GlassA11y
target: if a preferences panel is wanted, a small GlassPreferencesPanel bound to the redesigned AccessibilityProvider
justification: It is 1,124 lines of demoware: mocked test results, a hard-coded AAA claim, a no-op detect button, an advertised shortcut that does not exist, stale-closure settings panels that reset each other, and a panel that becomes invisible under reduced motion. It is the opposite of what an accessibility component should be. Its look depends on Tailwind classes the library does not ship and on story-level !important overrides. Remove it, or rebuild a small honest preferences panel on top of a real provider.

name: GlassHighContrast / GlassMotionControls / GlassScreenReader / GlassKeyboardNav (GlassA11y sub-panels)
target: GlassSwitch/GlassSelect inside a rebuilt preferences panel
justification: These are internal pieces of a fake panel, leaked to the root export. They hand-roll switches instead of using GlassSwitch and have uneven a11y.

name: GlassFocusIndicators
target: token-driven :focus-visible ring in base CSS + src/primitives/focus/{SkipLinks,FocusTrap,GlassFocusScope}
justification: This component makes accessibility worse. It hijacks global shortcuts, blurs focus on Escape anywhere, leaks focus-trap listeners, restyles every focusable element through a side-effect CSS import, keeps skip links invisible when focused and hides its ring under reduced motion. Its overlay positioning classes do not exist. The primitives/focus folder already has proper SkipLinks and FocusTrap. A premium system needs one well-designed token :focus-visible ring in base CSS, not a JS-tracked overlay.

name: BrandColorIntegration
target: theme tokens / ThemeProvider brand accent API
justification: It does not integrate brand colors: the 'API' is a mock lookup table of three trademarks, the generated CSS is invalid for its own default values, a global unscoped <style> tag leaks across instances, and the button ignores the variables it is supposed to consume. The certification screenshot is just a story-styled neutral card with two buttons. Brand accent belongs in the token/theme layer, not a runtime component.

name: GlassAchievementDashboard
justification: Fixed-position Tailwind panel hard-wired to the achievement engine; not a reusable design-system component.

name: GlassAchievementNotifications
target: GlassToast
justification: A bespoke toast that disappears before it can be read and is invisible under reduced motion; the library already has a toast system.

name: GlassAchievementSystem
justification: Gamification XP engine is product logic, not design-system surface. Visual output in the certification shot is a generic stat card with zero/one placeholder values; the dashboard is a fixed-position Tailwind-styled panel; notifications are inaccessible (700ms auto-dismiss, invisible under reduced motion). Module-level state mutation is a correctness bug. If a toast/achievement pattern is needed, build it from GlassToast + a Badge.

name: GlassAutoComposer (only useAutoComposer root-exported)
justification: Pure theater: keyword->template strings dressed up as LLM generation and a genetic optimizer, with a root export (useAutoComposer) that cannot function because its provider is not exported. Nothing here belongs in a premium design system.

name: GlassBiometricAdaptation
justification: Fake biometrics (invented bpm), leaking global listeners and intervals, invalid color math, and a privacy-hostile premise. Certification screenshot shows a static 'Initializing / Stress level 0%' card. No path to a premium component.

name: GlassBiometricDashboard
justification: One of four near-identical fixed 'engine dashboards' surfacing fake data.

name: GlassStressResponsive
justification: Adapts UI to a fabricated stress signal; nested surfaces; noisy live region.

name: GlassContextAware
target: interactive/ContextAwareGlass (or nothing)
justification: Claims environment-driven intensity but computes from constants and clock hour, writes CSS vars nobody reads, and re-renders on every mouse move. Third of at least four context/environment adaptive wrappers.

name: GlassContextualDashboard
justification: Duplicate floating engine dashboard over fabricated data.

name: GlassContextualEngine
justification: Requests geolocation on a timer, leaks intervals and memory, and dresses random-weight math as sensor fusion. A production hazard (privacy prompts, unbounded growth) with no visual value.

name: AdaptiveGlass
target: OptimizedGlass
justification: A thin material surface that duplicates OptimizedGlass with a broken `as` prop and side-effecting environment mutation.

name: EnvironmentalGlass
justification: weatherAPI=true picks random weather (Math.random) — fake; animates CSS filter brightness over content including text.

name: GlassColorTinting
justification: Named 'color tinting' but by design discards chroma; 'content-aware' just counts tags. Misleading name; folds into material density.

name: GlassEngine
target: primitives/OptimizedGlass + createGlassStyle (single material primitive)
justification: The only file here with a principled material model (canonical blur ladder, clamped neutral alpha, protected material keys). That logic should be folded into the core material primitive; the provider/environment/weather layer and the demo export should be dropped.

name: GlassEngineDemo
justification: A demo screen exported from the package root.

name: GlassOpacityEngine
target: OptimizedGlass (interactive density prop)
justification: Hover/scroll/time-driven alpha on a neutral surface; opacityRange default array literal in effect deps re-binds listeners every render; aria-label passed in demo is not accepted/forwarded.

name: GlassTextureVariations
justification: Calls updateConfig on the shared provider, so one instance changes the texture of every sibling surface.

name: GlassEyeTracking
justification: Loads remote code to access the camera, has a hook call inside an event handler that breaks calibration, is mouse-only, and its default state is a permanent 'Initializing' card. Not appropriate for a design system.

name: GlassEyeTrackingCalibration
justification: Part of the eye-tracking subsystem recommended for removal.

name: GlassGazeResponsive
justification: Part of the eye-tracking subsystem recommended for removal.

name: GlassGazeVisualization
justification: Part of the eye-tracking subsystem recommended for removal.

name: GlassFoldableSupport
target: layout primitives + CSS viewport-segment media queries in docs
justification: Wrong/deprecated APIs, a permission prompt on mount, and a reduced-motion bug that hides all content. Foldable support should be a documented CSS pattern, not a runtime component.

name: GlassLiquidTransition
target: animations/GlassTransitions (single transition/morph API on motion tokens)
justification: Broken forwardRef, a variant that hides its own content, inconsistent reduced-motion handling and landmark spam. A morph-on-hover primitive is reasonable but should live in one motion module with tokenized springs.

name: GlassLiveCursorPresence
target: collaboration/GlassCollaborativeCursor
justification: Third collaborative-cursor implementation; codemod-garbage classNames, invisible cursors under reduced motion, leaking reconnect timers. Keep one presence component wired to the shared collaboration service.

name: GlassMagneticCursor
target: GlassMagneticButton (element-level magnetism)
justification: Global cursor replacement is an a11y anti-pattern for a design system; element-level magnetism already exists in GlassMagneticButton. The certification image is a static placeholder, not the effect.

name: GlassMeshGradient
target: single AmbientBackground primitive (CSS/WebGL) under backgrounds/
justification: An ambient backdrop is genuinely useful behind glass (glass needs something to refract), but this one is colorless by default, blank under reduced motion, CPU-heavy (blur(100px) filter on a per-frame canvas) and duplicated by several atmospheric components. Rebuild as one tokenized, static-first ambient background with optional motion.

name: GlassMetaDashboard (GlassMetaEngine alias not root-exported)
justification: Fabricated 'system intelligence' (hard-coded health percentages, quantum/neural theater) with server-side interval leaks from render-time construction. Remove; real perf telemetry belongs in devtools, not the component package.

name: GlassNeuroFeedback
target: GlassProgress/GlassMeter
justification: An unlabeled progress bar bound to fake neuro data; a real Meter component should cover this.

name: GlassNeuroMetricsDashboard
justification: Pseudo-BCI with a crashing simulator, fake 'connected' state for real devices, and a certification screenshot that is literally blank. Remove.

name: GlassOrientationEffects
target: optional tilt option on a single interactive surface primitive
justification: Hides consumer content behind a permission prompt on ordinary desktops (visible in its own certification screenshot), ignores reduced motion, and its named effects are static overlays.

name: GlassParallaxLayers
justification: The concept (stacked glass planes at depth) is on-brand and the motion/reduced-motion work is decent, but hooks-in-loop, aria-hidden-by-default, and the silently ignored depth blur mean it does not deliver its premise. Rebuild with a per-layer child component (hooks legal), real per-depth blur tokens, and content-visible semantics.

name: GlassParticles
target: backgrounds/ParticleBackground (one particle field)
justification: One of four particle systems; hard-coded dark canvas defeats theming, defaults are invisible, and the certification capture shows no particle field. Merge the reduced-motion static-frame logic into a single tokenized particle background.

name: GlassPerformanceOptimization
target: Single headless quality-tier system in core (useGlassQualityTier + CSS custom-property tiers, @media prefers-reduced-transparency/reduced-motion), merged with GlassProgressiveEnhancement and hooks/useGlassOptimization
justification: Eight public exports that look like a performance framework but switch nothing: every tier returns the same createGlassStyle output, and the 'CPU' metric is an fps proxy driven by an uncancelled rAF loop that itself costs performance. Adaptive degradation is a real need for a glass system, but it belongs in one token/CSS-level tier mechanism, not in wrapper components with leaks. Replace with a core tier hook, then deprecate these exports with aliases for one major version.

name: GlassPredictiveEngine
justification: Marketed as an AI engine but it is a random-weight perceptron with broken training, threshold-based 'insights', and silent localStorage behavioural logging. Its only UI is an emoji FAB whose panel becomes invisible under reduced motion. A design system should not ship this; if predictive prefetch is wanted, it belongs in an app-level analytics package, not in aura-glass.

name: GlassProgressiveEnhancement
target: Core quality-tier system (with GlassPerformanceOptimization and hooks/useGlassOptimization); keep only the capability-detection logic, drop EnhancedGlass
justification: This is the only tier implementation with real capability detection, so its detection logic is worth salvaging. As shipped, though, it is not exported, mutates body/root globally, auto-degrades permanently, and its main component carries a broken className. Fold the detection into the single core tier provider, scoped to a root element rather than document.body.

name: GlassQuantumStates
justification: Pseudo-physics that randomises a button's meaning, crashes on click via a hook call inside an event handler, never initialises because of effect ordering, and leaks intervals. Only the useQuantumStates hook is root-exported, and it returns a no-op default context. There is nothing to salvage. Remove it together with the src/components/quantum family review.

name: GlassReactions
target: One Reactions family (ReactionBar + ReactionPicker popover + optional floating burst overlay) merged with src/components/interactive/GlassReactionBar and src/components/social/GlassReactionBubbles
justification: A legitimate pattern with real, if crude, physics. It is undermined by a global digit-key hijack, right-click-only discovery, an inaccessible menu, and content that vanishes under reduced motion. Three reaction components exist with a name collision on GlassReactionBar. Merge them into one accessible family (popover with roving focus, scoped shortcuts, opacity-only reduced-motion variant).

name: GlassSelfHealingSystem
target: Dev-only diagnostics in src/tools/GlassDevTools (axe + real contrast checks), not a runtime component
justification: Claims automatic visual and a11y repair but every fix is a no-op timer, and the diagnosis can recurse forever while burning a MutationObserver per wrapper in production. Runtime 'self-healing' is the wrong abstraction for a design system. Correctness belongs in build-time lint, tests and devtools.

name: GlassSpatialAudio
target: Single opt-in non-visual audio-feedback service (useGlassSound) merged with src/utils/soundDesign, shipped from a subpath, default off
justification: The only file in this shard with a genuine browser-API implementation. A provider-effect bug, though, guarantees no sound plays once initialised, AudioContexts leak, and the visual exports (visualizer, audio-reactive) are debug toys. Keep one small, opt-in sound service with a mute/consent API and drop the visual components.

name: GlassTrophyCase
target: src/components/advanced/GlassAchievementSystem (rebuild on GlassCard + GlassModal + GlassBadge with real tier tokens)
justification: A plausible product pattern, but tier identity is erased (all greys), colour-alpha math produces invalid CSS, opacity classes are flattened by a global attribute selector, and cards plus the modal are not keyboard-accessible. It duplicates the root-exported GlassAchievementSystem and is not itself exported. Merge into one achievement gallery composed from existing primitives.

name: GlassWebGLShader
target: One WebGL effect primitive (with LiquidGlassGPU) under an /effects or /three subpath; fix GLSL const loops, resize/DPR, sample a real backdrop or rename to a gradient shader
justification: The only real shader code in the library, but two of its five variants cannot compile on spec-conformant WebGL, it never refracts actual content, and the certified screenshot is its fallback panel with debug copy. It duplicates LiquidGlassGPU's goal. Merge into one well-engineered shader surface, or demote to a decorative 'GlassShaderBackground'.

name: IntelligentColorSystem
target: Brand/accent API in src/theme/ThemeProvider (scoped CSS vars on a theme root, OKLCH-based accessible ramps); rebuild BrandColorIntegration on it
justification: A provider that silently overwrites core text and background tokens on :root, creates a cyclic --glass-text-primary in dark mode, and shifts colours by time and season is a correctness hazard for every consumer. Its adaptive math cannot parse its own palette values. Theming must be deterministic and scoped, so remove this and move brand-colour input into the ThemeProvider.

name: LiquidGlassGPU
target: OptimizedGlass / a single Liquid Glass material primitive (CSS + optional SVG-filter refraction); any real WebGL path merges into the consolidated shader primitive with GlassWebGLShader
justification: Named after the library's core promise ('Liquid Glass'), but structurally it can never reach its GPU path and always shows a hard-coded CSS fallback. Its own header admits it is a demo. Shipping it from the root misleads users about what the material system is. Deprecate it with an alias to the real material primitive and remove it in 5.x.

name: LivingEcosystemSimulator
target: examples/ recipe (domain dashboard composed from GlassCard + GlassProgress + GlassBadge)
justification: Honest, small and built on the right primitive, but it is domain-specific demo content (habitats, biodiversity) with a misleading 'simulator / real-time' name, and it depends on Tailwind utilities the package does not ship. It belongs in examples as a composition recipe, not in the public component API.

name: MolecularBondingInterface
target: examples/ (if kept at all)
justification: A chemistry-themed list pair with no actual bonding visualization, whose only colour coding depends on Tailwind classes the library does not provide. It has no reusable value as a design-system component.

name: MultiDimensionalGestureRecognizer
justification: Named a gesture recognizer, but it recognises nothing: it is three clickable description cards with an ARIA 'application' role that harms screen-reader users. A real gesture primitive (if needed) should be a headless hook (usePointerGesture) next to GlassGestureZone.

name: StorybookVisualShowcase
justification: Dead code whose only historical purpose was to stand in for real components in visual certification with pre-written 'AA / no clipping / reduced motion' claims. Delete it, and add a CI guard that fails if a story renders a surrogate rather than its declared component.

name: AIGlassThemeProvider
target: src/theme/ThemeProvider (if any adaptive behavior is wanted, add a real token-mapping API there)
justification: The provider is labeled 'AI', but it picks a random hue after a fake delay, and the theme it produces is never connected to the token system, so nothing on screen changes. It also wraps consumer children in a decorated div, which a provider should never do. It is exported from the root, so removing it is a breaking change. Deprecate it in 4.x and remove it in 5.0. Adaptive theming belongs in the real ThemeProvider and token pipeline.

name: AIDemo
target: docs/examples (outside the published package)
justification: This is an example application, not a component. It ships an auth form, emoji tabs and localhost endpoints, and it calls OpenAI/Pinecone/Vision through a bespoke client, which conflicts with the Kiro Prism default-LLM policy. It is not exported, but it lives in src/ and Storybook certifies it as a visual target. Move it to an examples app, or delete it.

name: GlassDeepDreamGlass
justification: This is a 1,057-line demo that pretends to be a neural network: random activations and sine-wave pixel tints. The material uses ignored variants and className bugs, the panels remount and lose focus, and nothing here belongs in a premium design-system screenshot. It shares a before/after canvas shell with four sibling 'AI' components. Remove it. If a creative-tool showcase is wanted, build one honest ImageCompare/BeforeAfter primitive instead.

name: GlassGANGenerator
justification: This is a fake GAN: blobs and random losses, a prop-mutation bug, mouse-only cards, a download button that is dead and invisible, and images that disappear under reduced motion. It has no product value and actively damages the library's credibility. Remove it.

name: GlassGenerativeArt
justification: This is a mock text-to-image tool that names real vendors (Midjourney, DALL-E). Its prompt-enhancement toggle is broken, and canvas color stops are CSS variables, which are invalid for canvas and break generation. It is misleading and buggy. Remove it.

name: GlassIntelligentFormBuilder
target: aura-glass/workflows or a recipes package: 'FormSchemaBuilder' built on the library's form primitives
justification: This is the only component in the AI shard with a real use case: a schema editor with live preview. But it is a page-sized widget with broken label semantics, an h1 inside a component, mouse-only row selection, non-existent cyan utility classes, and an 'AI' label that is regex heuristics behind a timeout. Drop the AI branding and rebuild it on the official Field/Label/Select primitives as a recipe. Do not keep it in the core component set.

name: GlassLiveFilter
target: (optional) a small ImageFilterPreview recipe using CSS filter() instead of CPU loops
justification: The filters work, but they belong to an image-editing app, not a glass design system. The component leaks global CSS into sibling components, overrides core tokens, has a stale-closure bug in parameter updates, mouse-only tiles, and placebo GPU/FPS settings. It is off-mission for AuraGlass 5. Remove it from the core package.

name: GlassMusicVisualizer
target: src/components/media/GlassAdvancedAudioPlayer (extract a single AudioSpectrum/visualizer sub-component under media/)
justification: This is the one 'AI' component with real functionality, and it is not AI. The default colour scheme renders no bars because of hex-alpha concatenation on rgba/hsl(var()) strings. It re-renders 60 times per second, and it injects !important global-ish styles. Fold a corrected canvas spectrum (palette from tokens, no per-frame setState, a keyboard play control) into the media audio player family and delete this standalone copy.

name: GlassStyleTransfer
justification: The output does not depend on the input, so this is a placeholder posing as a feature. It also has broken gradient classes and asset URLs that 404. Remove it.

name: NeuralWeightVisualization
target: a generic GlassHeatmap/MatrixTable data-display component (diverging colour scale from tokens)
justification: This is a weight-matrix table whose visual encoding is absent: positive, negative and strong values all get the same white wash. Its styling relies on Tailwind classes the package does not ship. The legitimate need is a token-driven diverging heatmap/matrix in data-display. Replace it with that and drop the neural branding.

name: NeuromorphicLearningNetwork
justification: This is four stat cards with pseudo-scientific copy and a duplicate-callback bug. The library already has stat/KPI components. Remove it.

name: ProductionAIIntegration
target: separate server/example package (and route LLM calls through Kiro Prism if kept anywhere)
justification: This is a backend-integration demo shipped in a UI component tree. It pulls in Sentry and Node Buffer, and it has a path that could put an API key into a client bundle. Its dynamic imports cannot resolve once published, it has unlabeled inputs, and it calls providers directly in conflict with the Prism-first policy. It is not exported, but Storybook certifies it. Delete it from src/components.

name: AdvancedAnimations
target: src/tokens motion tokens (easing curves as cubic-bezier tokens) + docs page; drop the demo component
justification: This is a demo component with no product use. The easing table is duplicated in GlassMotionController and in the design tokens. Move the curves that are actually needed (as cubic-bezier motion tokens) into the token package, fix or delete shatterEase/glassEase, and remove the component.

name: GlassMotionController (+ GlassAnimated, GlassAnimationSequence, GlassAnimationTimeline, useMotionController, animationPresets)
target: src/animations/orchestration + MotionPreferenceProvider (single motion API on framer-motion; keep presets as motion tokens)
justification: This is a third, parallel animation system next to framer-motion and the library's own orchestration hooks. It has real bugs (never-resolving yoyo/infinite promises, a likely sequence re-fire loop) and spams screen readers on every animation. It is a root export, so deprecate it with re-export shims in 4.x and point users to the orchestration hooks and MotionPreferenceProvider. Move animationPresets into motion tokens.

name: GlassTransitions
target: src/components/advanced/GlassLiquidTransition (single transition primitive); move variants to motion tokens; delete the shadow Modal/Tabs/Accordion
justification: The transition primitive does not run its enter animation, and the page-transition wrapper never triggers. The module also smuggles in second implementations of Modal, Tabs and Accordion that are weaker than the real ones. Merge the variant definitions (fixed: keyed presence, initial/animate/exit wired, reduced-motion fallback to opacity-only) into GlassLiquidTransition and delete the rest.

name: GlassTransitions.GlassModal / GlassTabs / GlassAccordion / SwipeableGlassCards (static members)
target: real GlassModal / GlassTabs / GlassAccordion
justification: These are weaker, inaccessible clones of first-class components. Under reduced motion they become invisible: the modal blocks the page with nothing visible, and accordion and tab content never appears. Delete them from the GlassTransitions namespace.

name: OrganicAnimationEngine (+ GentleAnimation, EnergeticAnimation, InteractiveAnimation, ContemplativeAnimation, COMMON_SEQUENCES)
target: framer-motion variants + motion tokens; EnhancedGlassButton should use a reduced-motion-aware hover/press primitive
justification: It ignores prefers-reduced-motion while running infinite loops, has a timer-compounding auto-trigger bug, fires on every scroll, and its 'physics/emotion/adaptive' features are cosmetic. It leaks into the root via EnhancedGlassButton. Remove it and migrate EnhancedGlassButton to the shared press/hover motion.

name: ARGlassEffects (R3F implementation)
justification: This is a mock WebXR experience. It fires fake interaction events, never animates (unattached material refs), leaks materials, and crashes on portal click through a hook called inside a callback. It is the opposite of production 'Liquid Glass'. Remove it. If spatial work continues, start from a real WebXR session hook in a lab package.

name: ARGlassEffects (lazy wrapper + fallback)
target: aura-glass/three lab subpath (experimental) or remove with ARGlassEffects.r3f
justification: The lazy-load pattern is the one good idea here and should become the shared template for 3D modules. But the visible fallback paints nothing, because its styling classes do not exist, and the real implementation behind it is a mock (see the r3f record). Deprecate it along with its implementation.

name: GlassAuroraDisplay
target: AuroraPro / marketing AuroraBackground
justification: A demo toy, not a design-system component: a canvas science-fair simulation with dead controls, invalid canvas fonts, per-frame React re-renders, fixed 800px width, and a certification capture that is essentially a near-black rectangle (canvas region max channel saturation 25/255, i.e. no visible aurora bands) with a debug info box. Aurora as a brand surface already exists in AuroraPro and marketing/AuroraBackground; this one adds nothing a premium system should ship.

name: GlassBiomeSimulator
justification: A 1.3k-line canvas toy that someone has partly restyled (neutral palettes, nice switch controls) but which remains a simulation demo with dead props, per-frame React re-render, invalid canvas colors and bespoke inline material that bypasses the glass primitives. It has no place in a component library's public surface; if a demo is desired it belongs in the docs site, not the npm package. The control styling (switch, range thumb) is the only salvageable part and should be implemented once in the real Switch/Slider components.

name: GlassNebulaClouds
justification: Worst-in-shard: entirely non-functional controls, per-frame random star strobing, re-created rAF loop each frame, invalid canvas colors, fixed pixel size, and a palette deliberately neutralised to grey so it no longer even reads as a nebula (certification screenshot average saturation 2.4/255). Nothing here is reusable design-system material.

name: GlassWeatherGlass
justification: Technically the least-broken atmospheric canvas (refs, DPR, responsive), but it is still a demo simulation with dead toggles, wasteful per-frame allocation and grey 'rainbows'; the screenshot is almost uniformly pale grey (mean luminance 243, saturation 0.6). Four sibling canvas simulations share copy-pasted particle code; none belong in the package. If weather-reactive ambience is wanted, it should be a token-driven background preset, not a 1k-line canvas.

name: AtmosphericBackground
target: single <GlassBackdrop preset=...> (merge with DynamicAtmosphere + marketing/AuroraBackground)
justification: Small and SSR-safe, but it is one of at least four overlapping 'ambient gradient background' components, has an unimplemented blur prop, and its default output is a near-invisible pale wash (screenshot mean luminance 243, saturation 2.0). A premium system needs exactly one backdrop/ambient-light component with token-driven presets that are tuned to make glass read; fold this into that.

name: DynamicAtmosphere (GlassDynamicAtmosphere)
target: single <GlassBackdrop preset=...> (this file is the best base)
justification: The most reasonable of the background family: SSR-stable seeded particles, CSS-driven animation, canonical blur ladder via createGlassStyle. It should become the base of one consolidated backdrop component, after removing unimplemented modes (audio/time), unused props (intent/elevation/tier/particleElement), moving the gradient computation into render (no first-paint flash), and fixing applyAlpha so intensity works on token colors (color-mix for all inputs).

name: ParticleBackground
target: single particle effect (one of GlassParticles / GlassParticleField / ParticleBackground) or the GlassBackdrop preset
justification: Generic 2015-era 'particles.js' connected-dots effect -- the opposite of the premium Liquid Glass bar -- with an rAF loop restarted on every mouse move, fake CSS-variable color parsing, role=img hiding children, and a focusable decorative background. At least four particle components exist; keep at most one, rebuilt with stable loop, DPR, token colors and aria-hidden decoration.

name: EnhancedGlassButton
target: GlassButton
justification: Marketing-driven fake complexity: 'biometric' and 'emotional' adaptation derived from Math.random, a default physics wrapper, broken ref forwarding, and a 3.6k-line static dependency graph for a button. It forks the material and sizing scales from GlassButton, undermining consistency. Delete it (and its five preset wrappers); any genuinely useful press/ripple physics should be a small opt-in prop on GlassButton.

name: GlassButton
justification: The library's most important primitive and the right flagship slot, but today it is a 1.4k-line grab-bag: variants silently collapse to identical neutral glass because defaulted props shadow the variant table, fullWidth is broken by an inline-block wrapper div, reduced motion is read but ignored, conditional hooks violate the Rules of Hooks, and five 'consciousness' engines are bundled into every button. Redesign as a lean (~250 line) button: render the button itself as root (no wrapper), one colour axis (variant/intent), 3-4 sizes with >=44px touch targets, motion gated by reduced motion, and move consciousness features out entirely.

name: Non-exported internals (GlassButton.tsx/GlassFab.tsx/EnhancedGlassButton.tsx/GlassCalendar.tsx/card index)
target: Keep IconButton (export from root, built on redesigned GlassButton); delete the rest
justification: Dead-weight duplicates and marketing presets that are unreachable from the public entry but still compiled and shipped in dist via the files that define them. IconButton should be promoted and root-exported; everything else should be removed, and card/index.ts must stop exporting `any` stubs that shadow the real typed subcomponents.

name: GlassFab
target: GlassButton (shape='fab' / a thin GlassFab wrapper over the redesigned button)
justification: Two FABs exist (this and GlassButton's FloatingActionButton); this one has its own size vocabulary, solid non-glass fills, double material, removed focus outline and a hover-only tooltip. Rebuild as a ~60 line positioning/shape wrapper over the redesigned GlassButton and the library Tooltip.

name: MagneticButton (GlassMagneticButton)
target: GlassButton magnetic prop (OptimizedGlass already exposes `magnet`)
justification: A thin effect wrapper whose headline parameter (radius) does not work because pull is gated on hover, with an unused damping prop, matchMedia in render and double wrapper divs. GlassButton already passes `magnet` to OptimizedGlass; expose one properly implemented magnetic option there and delete this component.

name: LiquidGlassButtonStyle
target: GlassButton (material='liquid' as the default Liquid Glass button)
justification: The cleanest code in the button folder, and closest to the 'Liquid Glass' direction, but it duplicates GlassButton's material='liquid' path, kills the focus outline, and puts className on the wrong element. Its simplicity (one primitive, a native button) is exactly what the redesigned GlassButton should look like; merge it in and delete it. No certification screenshot exists.

name: GlassCalendar
target: shared Calendar grid primitive used by GlassDatePicker
justification: A calendar is a credibility component; this one lacks grid semantics and arrow-key navigation, ignores locale for weekdays/week start, advertises unimplemented week/day views, uses Tailwind default palette for events, and is wired to stub Card subcomponents. The certification capture is a small, low-contrast grey grid (saturation 0.2). Redesign as one accessible calendar-grid primitive (role=grid, roving focus, Intl weekday names, firstDayOfWeek) shared with GlassDatePicker; drop the decorative event list or make it a separate composition.

name: div (card/div.tsx)
target: GlassCard
justification: An accidental artifact (likely a codemod that rewrote <Card> to <div>) that adds a third conflicting set of Card subcomponents and a story/certification target named 'div'. Not root-exported; delete it along with its story/test and the stub exports in card/index.ts.

name: GlassCardLink
target: GlassCard with asChild/href (or interactive/GlassCardLink if kept)
justification: Two different components named GlassCardLink exist; the root export points at this one, which renders no glass, has no ref forwarding and no router integration. Replace with GlassCard supporting asChild/href so a link card is a glass card.

name: GlassCard
justification: Solid bones -- shared primitive, real keyboard/role handling, reduced motion actually wired -- making it the best flagship candidate in this shard. It needs polish, not rewrite: delete the redundant utility stack and junk overlay class strings, collapse 8 variants to ~4 (plain/elevated/outlined/interactive), remove blue hover shadow and 5% scale, add asChild, export the typed subcomponents from root and delete the card/index.ts stubs and card/div.tsx copy. Certification capture shows a small, faint card on a white canvas (saturation 0.1) -- the story needs a backdrop that lets glass read.

name: GlowingCard
target: GlassCard glow/emphasis prop (token-driven accent edge light)
justification: Neon/rainbow glow is the 'generic glassmorphism template' look the premium bar rejects, implemented with a global per-instance style injection and dropped props. Its single story even neutralises the glow, so the certified screenshot proves nothing. If an emphasised card is needed, make it a token-driven edge-light/emphasis option on GlassCard.

name: Card patterns (BasicCard, FeatureCard, StatCard, ProfileCard, NotificationCard, PricingCard, ActivityCard)
target: docs recipes / dashboard GlassStatCard / marketing ShowcaseCard
justification: Useful as documentation recipes showing GlassCard composition, but as library API they are not root-exported, duplicate dedicated dashboard/marketing cards, and use emoji icons, Tailwind default status colours and an unlabeled dismiss button. Move them to docs examples built on the polished GlassCard and the icon set; do not ship as components.

name: AtmosphericEffects
justification: Orphaned (only reference is commented out in ModularGlassDataChart.tsx:940-944 and 987-993), invisible in its own certification screenshot because of zIndex:-1, and its animation strategy (setState every rAF frame) is a performance anti-pattern. Background atmospherics already exist in a dedicated family; charts should not ship their own particle system.

name: ChartAxis
justification: A demo stub with no data input, unused anywhere in source (only re-exported from charts/components/index.ts), and its certification screenshot is effectively empty yet marked 'passed'. A real axis belongs inside the unified chart engine with a scale API.

name: ChartContainer (charts/components)
justification: One of five chart-container implementations, unused, and its core background declaration is a quoting bug that ships an invalid CSS value. Chart frames should use the shared surface primitive (OptimizedGlass/GlassCard) once.

name: ChartFilters
justification: Global hard-coded filter IDs (chart-glow, chart-blur, chart-gradient-0...) collide as soon as two instances or palettes exist on a page, and its only consumer has it commented out. GlassDataChart separately duplicates the same idea; neither is applied to a canvas renderer anyway.

name: ChartGrid
target: Unified SVG chart engine (single Grid primitive driven by the scale ticks used by GlassChart)
justification: The only sub-primitive that is approximately correct (useId, token-ish color), but it is disconnected from data and unused. Its logic should move into the one chart engine so grid lines align with real ticks.

name: ChartLegend (charts/components)
target: Single public ChartLegend (toggle buttons with aria-pressed, keyboard support) consumed by every chart
justification: Seven different legend implementations exist in this shard alone. This one is unused, keyboard-broken despite announcing role=button, and visually tiny. Keep one legend with real button semantics and shared material.

name: ChartRenderer
justification: Internal-only, has a blank certification screenshot that was marked passed, and its ref contract is wrong (passes a div), which breaks the only consumer's hover/export. It also duplicates GlassDataChart's chart.js wrapper. Remove along with ModularGlassDataChart.

name: ChartTooltip
target: Single chart tooltip built on the shared GlassTooltip/positioning primitive
justification: Six tooltip variants exist across the chart family. This one is opaque, unclamped, drops zero values, and ignores half its props. Merge into one positioned, glass-material tooltip.

name: KpiChart
target: src/components/dashboard/GlassKPICard.tsx
justification: A minimal KPI tile that duplicates the dashboard KPI card, with dead animation props and a token misuse that produces an invalid margin. Fold it into GlassKPICard.

name: GlassAreaChart
target: Redesigned GlassChart (single SVG engine, type='area')
justification: Functional SVG area chart with stacking, but its animations reference non-existent keyframes, axis titles are invisible because of HTML-in-SVG, it stretches via preserveAspectRatio='none', and it shares most of its code with GlassLineChart. Merge Line/Area/Bar/Pie into one scale-based engine with responsive measurement, then polish the material there.

name: GlassBarChart
target: Redesigned GlassChart (single SVG engine, type='bar')
justification: Bars cannot be reached by keyboard, axis text is tuned for dark surfaces and disappears on light ones, data labels do not render, and the grow animation does not exist. Its grouping math is reusable inside a unified engine.

name: GlassChart (+ ConsciousGlassChart, PredictiveGlassChart, AdaptiveGlassChart, ImmersiveGlassChart, withChartConsciousness, ChartConsciousnessPresets)
target: Becomes the single public chart API: one SVG/scale engine with type='line|area|bar|pie|donut|scatter', a real legend/tooltip, a data-table fallback, no consciousness layer
justification: Most of the 2,163 lines are theatre: consciousness hooks that do nothing, conditional hook calls, no-op magnetic/depth/performance stubs, placeholder tabs, a no-op download, and a role='img' that hides its own controls. The idea of one facade over chart types is right, and it is the natural flagship slot after a rewrite, but nothing in this implementation should be carried forward except the data normalisation helpers (normalizePoint, transformChartJsData).

name: GlassDataChart (also exported as DataChart)
target: Redesigned GlassChart (optionally a thin, opt-in chart.js adapter on a separate subpath, e.g. aura-glass/charts-chartjs)
justification: It renders a usable canvas chart with a decent header, but about half the advertised surface (toolbar, export, type switching, KPI, zoom, physics) is unreachable or stubbed, and it mutates global Chart.js defaults at import time, which is unacceptable for a library. Deprecate in favour of the unified engine; if canvas rendering is needed for large datasets, ship it as an opt-in adapter without global mutation.

name: GlassLineChart (+ GlassChartContainer)
target: Redesigned GlassChart (single SVG engine, type='line')
justification: The most usable of the SVG trio, but it is a copy of GlassAreaChart minus the fill, with the same dead animations, distortion and missing keyboard access. Merge into one engine; drop GlassChartContainer (yet another container).

name: GlassPieChart (+ GlassDonutChart)
target: Redesigned GlassChart (type='pie'|'donut')
justification: Visually the strongest chart in the shard, but a single 100% segment renders nothing (an arc whose start and end points coincide), donut center text does not render, the tooltip is mis-positioned, and segments are not reachable by keyboard. Its arc math and legend-with-values layout are worth porting into the unified engine.

name: ModularGlassDataChart (+ Conscious/Predictive/Adaptive/ImmersiveModularGlassDataChart, ModularChartConsciousnessPresets)
justification: Not publicly exported, has no in-repo consumers, crashes on hover and export because of the div-as-chart ref, renders every legend item as disabled, and is a third copy of the chart.js wrapper plus the consciousness theatre. Its certification 'pass' is not credible given the textless screenshot.

name: ChartContainerStyles (ChartContainer, ChartHeader, ChartTitle, ChartSubtitle, createChartContainerStyles)
justification: Internal styling helper used only by ModularGlassDataChart (slated for removal); duplicates four other chart containers and drops its blur parameter. The createChartContainerStyles factory is dead.

name: ChartElementStyles (ChartToolbar, ChartTypeSelector, TypeButton, ToolbarButton, EnhancedExportButton, ChartLegend, LegendItem, LegendColor, LegendLabel, createChartElementStyles, getColorPalette)
target: Shared chart toolbar/legend primitives inside the redesigned GlassChart (use the library SegmentedControl/ToggleGroup for the type switch)
justification: Only ModularGlassDataChart uses these. The toolbar/legend markup is a reasonable starting point but duplicates GlassChart's module CSS and lacks pressed/focus states. Move the useful pieces into the unified chart and delete the dead factories.

name: TooltipStyles (GlassTooltipContainer, TooltipHeader/Body/Item/Label/Value/Separator/Footer, createTooltipStyles, calculateTooltipPosition, formatTooltipValue)
justification: 474 lines with zero importers anywhere in src (verified by rg). Pure dead weight that adds a sixth tooltip vocabulary.

name: GlassTypingIndicator
justification: The right shape for a chat primitive (OptimizedGlass, forwardRef, live region, small API), but the shipped CSS lacks the classes it depends on, so dots are transparent and do not bounce outside Storybook, and reduced motion is read and then ignored. Fix by moving dot color and animation to tokens and glass-* CSS (with a prefers-reduced-motion fallback to static dots), showing dots alongside the user text, and removing the runtime style injection. GlassPresenceIndicator should then reuse it.

name: GlassCanvas
justification: This canvas runs code with new Function(), puts all component data into inline styles, highlights every child when one is selected, has drop zones that never activate, and builds Tailwind classes at runtime that never get generated. It cannot be used from the keyboard, and it claims role=main. Polishing would not fix it. Remove it along with the CMS suite.

name: GlassComponentPalette
justification: This panel only works inside the GlassPageBuilder app. Its glass is hand-written inline rgba, it uses emoji as icons, and it can't be used from the keyboard. Nothing here can be reused that the library doesn't already offer better (search field, accordion, list). Remove it together with the CMS suite.

name: GlassDragDropProvider (DragDropProvider)
justification: The page-builder state engine has a stub move operation, mutates state in place, leaves property edits out of undo, can't be configured, and has no keyboard or touch drag-and-drop. It is application code, not a design-system primitive. If 5.0 wants drag-and-drop, it should provide a headless sortable primitive (or wrap dnd-kit) with proper keyboard semantics. This file is not a starting point for that.

name: GlassPageBuilder
justification: A design-system library should not ship a half-built page-builder application. Its public callbacks are never invoked, Publish is an alert(), keyboard shortcuts hijack Ctrl+S/Z/P and do nothing, the status bar is static text, and the underlying provider's moveComponent is a no-op so reordering silently fails. Its rendered button styling in certification comes from a story decorator with !important overrides, so the screenshot is not evidence of component quality. Combined with the new Function() script execution in GlassCanvas, this is a liability. If a builder is strategically wanted, it belongs in a separate example app built on real primitives (Toolbar, SegmentedControl, TreeView, Inspector), not in the 5.0 core package.

name: GlassPageStructure
justification: This is the fifth tree implementation in the library and the weakest one. It has no tree semantics, its row actions only appear on hover, every component shows a 'Hidden' badge because of a logic bug, and its import path is unvalidated. Remove it with the CMS suite, and point any tree need to the single consolidated TreeView.

name: GlassPropertyPanel
justification: It doesn't use the library's own form controls. None of its labels are attached to their inputs. It ships a field for entering JavaScript that gets executed, and it was only certified on its empty state. A premium design system should show an 'Inspector' pattern as a composed recipe of real GlassField components, not ship this.

name: CollaborativeGlassWorkspace
justification: This is a 1,547-line mock that ships in the root bundle. Its own header comment says it is a demo. Every action is a no-op, its user props are ignored, and its fake 'connected' state disagrees with the real provider it wraps (which may open a live socket). Exporting it from the package root signals capabilities that don't exist. At most it should move to a Storybook-only showcase or a docs example. Also: the inline <style> block is injected again for every instance, and WorkspaceFloatingActions/VoiceChatPanel/VersionControlPanel use glass-fixed (1332, 1381, 1441), so they escape any contained or compact host.

name: GlassTeamCursors
justification: A publicly exported component that can only draw three fake cursors. It has no data input. Remove it. Its cursor SVG (path at 1251) looks better than GlassCollaborativeCursor's, so it could be harvested into the consolidated cursor component.

name: GlassTeamCursorsWithEffects
justification: This is fake complexity. The 'ripple' and 'glow' it promises are two static circles at fixed coordinates, layered over three hard-coded fake cursors. Remove it.

name: GlassCollaborationDashboard
target: GlassPresence (single presence/avatar-stack + activity popover built on GlassAvatarGroup + GlassPopover/Tabs)
justification: A presence pill with an activity popover is a legitimate pattern, and this widget is the most coherent visual in the collaboration folder. But it overlaps with at least three other presence components, it injects fake users in production when data is empty, it computes status with Date.now() during render, and its tabs and toggles have no ARIA. Fold its layout into one consolidated GlassPresence that uses the library's Avatar, Popover and Tabs primitives, with demo data kept in stories only.

name: GlassCollaborationProvider (CollaborationProvider, useCollaboration)
target: headless presence adapter interface (subscribe/publish) consumed by a single GlassPresence/GlassCursors visual layer; transport supplied by consumer
justification: This is the only file in the collaboration folder that does real work. A design system should still not own a bespoke WebSocket protocol configured through env vars. For 5.0 it should become a thin, documented adapter contract (users, cursors, comments) with a reference in-memory adapter for docs. Real transports (Liveblocks/Yjs/PartyKit or the app's own) should plug in from outside. If the team does not want to maintain an adapter, it should be removed.

name: GlassCollaborativeComments
target: GlassCommentThread (interactive) + a positioned GlassAnnotationPin primitive
justification: Spatial comment pins are a valid pattern, but this version only works with a mouse. It drops comments silently in its default demo mode, credits every reply to the wrong author, and positions bubbles imperatively in a way that makes them jump. Merge the thread UI into GlassCommentThread. Pin positioning should become a small anchored-popover primitive that keyboard users can reach.

name: GlassCollaborativeCursor
target: single GlassCursors/GlassLiveCursorPresence (merge with advanced/GlassLiveCursorPresence and social/GlassCollaborativeCursor)
justification: At least four cursor-presence implementations exist, and two of them share this exact name. This one is small and data-driven, which makes it a reasonable base, but its labels have no glass treatment, motion ignores reduced-motion, and label contrast is not controlled. Keep one cursor component that takes container-relative coordinates, uses a glass label with contrast-safe text, and respects reduced motion. Delete the rest.

name: MultiUserGlassEditor
target: GlassTextarea + GlassPresence composition example
justification: Despite the name, this is a styled textarea with decorative chips. The presence dots are the same color for every state, the user colors are computed but never shown, and it falls back to fake users. No collaborative behavior exists. It was never certified with a screenshot. Remove it and document the composition (GlassTextarea + GlassPresence) as a recipe instead.

name: CompactCookieNotice
target: GlassCookieConsent variant='compact'
justification: This is the only cookie component that actually dismisses itself. It still has no decline path, which a consent UI needs for compliance, no ARIA semantics, a forced-black text override, and DOM prop leaks. Keep its compact layout as a variant of the consolidated consent component.

name: CookieConsent
target: GlassCookieConsent (single component: variant='compact'|'banner'|'preferences', controlled open/onOpenChange, shared consent store hook)
justification: Its token-based material and wired reduced-motion springs are the most systematic code in this shard. Functionally, though, it is broken: clicking Accept or Decline neither stores consent nor closes the banner, and there's no controlled prop to fix that from outside. It also has no dialog or region semantics and leaks unknown props onto the DOM. All three cookie components copy the same cookie helpers, position map and spring setup. Merge them into one GlassCookieConsent with variants, a useCookieConsent store, proper role and label attributes, and a working dismiss.

name: GlobalCookieConsent
target: GlassCookieConsent variant='preferences' (base of the consolidated component)
justification: This is the most complete of the three and reuses real primitives (GlassModal, GlassCheckbox, GlassButton), so it should be the base for the consolidated GlassCookieConsent. Before 5.0 it needs labelled checkboxes, a working details disclosure, dialog/region semantics, the mobile centering fix, cookies encoded with SameSite/Secure, an exit animation, and a consent-state hook. It's a utility pattern, not a showcase piece.

name: DimensionalDashboardContainer
target: surfaces/GlassDepthLayer (single depth/parallax primitive)
justification: A thin translateZ/tilt wrapper that re-renders on every animation frame and every mouse move, with unbounded scroll-driven translateZ and stacked absolute layers that are not usable as a dashboard container. Reduced-motion handling is one of the better ones in this shard, but the concept is duplicated by DimensionalGlass, GlassDepthLayer, GlassParallaxLayers and Glass3DEngine. Fold the tilt/depth behaviour into one depth primitive driven by CSS variables/motion values instead of React state.

name: GlassActivityFeed
target: merge with data-display/GlassTimeline as a single list primitive
justification: Dashboards need an activity feed, but this one flattens status semantics (all types styled the same), stacks a backdrop-filter on every row, overrides tokens with !important, has non-keyboard row actions, and has filter/pagination bugs in its default grouped mode. Rebuild it on a semantic list with rows that are a tokenised inner surface (no per-row blur), real status tones, and roving focus. Then share the row anatomy with GlassTimeline.

name: GlassChartWidget
target: templates/dashboard/widgets/ChartWidget + charts ChartContainer -> one GlassWidget/Panel with header actions slot
justification: A reasonable chart-frame idea, but it overlaps with the template ChartWidget, ChartContainer and WidgetGlass. Its menu and fullscreen are not accessible overlays, and the !important colour override breaks the series colours of any chart placed inside. Keep one dashboard panel primitive that uses the library's real Menu/Dialog primitives for actions and fullscreen.

name: GlassKPICard
target: single GlassStatCard (KPI/Metric/Stat merged) built on data-display/GlassMetricChip tokens
justification: This is roughly 80% the same code as GlassMetricCard and GlassStatCard (same size/variant tables, same skeleton, same trend block, same Grid helper), using raw Tailwind palette colours and purple hover glows that do not belong to a neutral glass system. Merge the three into one stat card with slots (trend, sparkline, progress, comparison) and token-driven status tones, then keep GlassKPICard as a deprecated alias.

name: GlassMetricCard
target: single GlassStatCard (use GlassMetricCard's forwardRef/HTMLAttributes API as the base)
justification: Its API is the strongest of the three stat cards, so it should be the base of the merged component. The progress bar still needs ARIA, the status palette needs tokens, the purple/blue hover glows should go, and the ref must forward in every branch.

name: GlassStatCard
target: single GlassStatCard (absorb KPI/Metric; replace sparkline with charts primitive)
justification: This is the third copy of the stat-card pattern. Its one differentiator, the sparkline, is geometrically broken: a 32px path coordinate space inside an 8px svg with pixel-not-percent x values. Keep the name for the merged component, but rebuild the sparkline on the charts package with a viewBox and accessible labelling.

name: NOTE: non-root or internal pieces in this shard
justification: Informational record only. Certification screenshots could not be rendered in this session (Read tool returned empty for PNG/JPEG), so visual scores are code-derived; certification JSON shows only the Default story was inspected per component, dark theme only, issuesFound=[] for all, and GlassEmptyState/GlassErrorState have no certification target.

name: GlassAccordion
target: Single compound Accordion (Root/Item/Trigger/Content) on a shared disclosure primitive; absorb GlassAccordionUI
justification: Accordion is a core primitive that must be flawless; this one uses tab semantics, has broken aria-labelledby, cross-instance focus via document.querySelector, a non-rotating (or double-rotating) chevron and inline rgba that overrides the glass primitive. Two accordions exist in the library. Rebuild once as a compound disclosure component with correct WAI-ARIA, scoped focus, inert closed panels and token-driven material, then retire GlassAccordionUI.

name: GlassAlert (+ GlassAlertTitle, GlassAlertDescription, GlassAlertActions; aliases Alert/AlertTitle/...)
justification: Structurally reasonable compound alert on the shared primitive. Needs: correct live-region semantics (role=status for non-urgent, alert only for errors), distinct info intent, controlled open + exit motion, configurable heading level, and removal of the leaked material-engine props. GlassErrorState should become an Alert recipe rather than a separate component.

name: GlassAnimatedNumber (+ GlassAnimatedCounter, GlassAnimatedStat, useAnimatedNumber)
target: Unstyled-by-default AnimatedNumber (typography only, Intl.NumberFormat, reduced-motion, aria-live final value) consumed by a single Metric/Stat component
justification: Counting numbers are a premium-feel detail, but this implementation puts a glass box around text, ignores reduced motion despite importing the hook, leaks a prop to the DOM, and lacks locale formatting. Redesign as a pure typographic primitive and fold Counter/Stat into the metric family.

name: GlassAvatar (+ GlassAvatarGroup, GlassAvatarFallback)
target: Compound Avatar (Root/Image/Fallback/Status) + single AvatarGroup; delete duplicate in interactive/
justification: Typing is internally contradictory (elevation), the public variant name is a CSS class, the ref disappears in fallback state, and a11y double-announces. Two AvatarGroups exist. Rebuild as a small compound primitive with Radix-style image loading status.

name: GlassBadge (+ StatusBadge, CountBadge, BadgeGroup)
target: One Badge primitive (non-interactive, tokenized tone scale, no backdrop-filter) + Tag/Chip for interactive; fold BadgeLine/BadgeCluster/StatusBadge into it
justification: A badge that renders all semantic tones identically and is a live region is broken at the most basic level. Per-badge backdrop-filter is wasteful for a 20px label. Redesign as a cheap, tokenized tone badge; interactive/removable behavior belongs to Chip.

name: GlassBadgeLine
target: Badge group pattern (BadgeGroup) in redesigned Badge
justification: A 73-line map over Tailwind classes the library does not ship. It is a strict subset of BadgeGroup and LiquidGlassBadgeCluster. Remove (or keep a deprecated alias to the consolidated Badge group for one major).

name: GlassChip (+ GlassChipGroup)
target: Chip/Tag (interactive: filter, input, choice) with ChipGroup using radio/checkbox group semantics; absorbs removable Badge
justification: Chips are high-frequency surfaces; this one has fake variants, forced dark text, nested interactive controls, wrong ARIA for single-select, sub-minimum remove target and default sound effects. Redesign into a proper filter/choice chip family with tokenized selected state.

name: GlassDataGrid
target: Single GlassTable/DataTable (headless sort/filter/selection + optional virtualization); reuse this file's CSS-module token approach
justification: Clean token-based CSS and decent keyboard sort, but it ships a fake drag-reorder feature with stub physics hooks and duplicates at least five other table implementations. Its styling approach should be the template for the consolidated table; the component itself should be merged.

name: GlassDataGridPro
target: GlassDataTable (consolidated)
justification: A placeholder that advertises Pro features (grouping) it does not implement, with a divergent prop vocabulary. Remove; provide a codemod/alias to the consolidated table.

name: GlassDataTable (+ ConsciousGlassDataTable, PredictiveDataTable, GazeResponsiveDataTable, AccessibleDataTable, DataTableConsciousnessPresets)
target: Single consolidated GlassTable: headless core (TanStack-style) + glass skin from GlassDataGrid.module.css; drop all consciousness variants
justification: A data table is a flagship-grade surface for a premium design system and this file has the right bones (typed columns, mobile card layout, pagination, selection). But it is weighed down by Rules-of-Hooks violations, a dropped ref, keyboard-inaccessible sorting, three competing material sources, dead Tailwind classes, 6k lines of pseudo-AI imports and fake eye-tracking/biometric presets. Rebuild as the one table for the library with controlled state, virtualization option and real a11y; delete the consciousness exports and the four sibling tables.

name: GlassDiffViewer
target: Shared CodeSurface primitive + DiffViewer using a real diff algorithm (e.g. jsdiff, pinned) with optional highlighter
justification: The name promises a diff viewer; the algorithm is wrong for any real-world change, and split mode does not show differences. Either implement a real line diff with hunks and split alignment on a shared code-surface primitive, or remove it from the core package.

name: GlassDivider (+ GlassTextDivider, GlassIconDivider)
target: GlassSeparator (layout) with a token hairline + optional label slot
justification: A divider should be a token hairline; this one has a combinatorial prop surface built on missing Tailwind classes, animates on mount, and duplicates GlassSeparator. Merge into one Separator with hairline/label variants.

name: GlassEmptyState
justification: Small, sane, recent component. Fix the forced dark text token, drop the live-region role, add heading-level/slot API, add tests and certification coverage (no screenshot exists), and make tables/kanban reuse it for their empty states.

name: GlassErrorState
target: StateView (empty/error/loading) family sharing one layout, or GlassAlert recipe
justification: Thin component with an invalid primitive prop and no danger styling. Merge with EmptyState/LoadingState into a single state-view component with tone tokens.

name: GlassGanttChart
target: Move to an optional @aura-glass/charts or labs package; not core
justification: A Gantt chart is an application, not a design-system component. This one misplaces child task dates, has no keyboard path, advertises unimplemented features and uses per-bar backdrop-filter. Deprecate out of core; if kept, rebuild in a labs package on a canvas/SVG renderer with a single glass container.

name: GlassHeatmap
target: Charts family on a shared viz layer (single SVG/canvas, tokenized sequential palettes, accessible data table fallback)
justification: Useful concept, but per-cell buttons without names, per-cell Motion staggering, nested glass layers and token-by-string-matching make it neither accessible nor scalable. Redesign within a coherent charts layer.

name: GlassJSONViewer
target: Shared CodeSurface/CodeBlock primitive (JSON as a language mode); collapsible tree as optional labs feature
justification: A 78-line styled <pre> with bespoke backdrop-filter and an unsafe stringify. Fold into one code-surface primitive shared with DiffViewer/SchemaViewer.

name: GlassKanbanBoard
target: Labs/templates package (merge with interactive/GlassKanban); core keeps only Card + sortable list primitives
justification: Board-level app widget with demo data baked in, no keyboard or touch drag, no insertion index, triple stacked backdrop-filters and a duplicate in interactive/. Move out of core into a templates/labs package built on a real accessible DnD layer (e.g. dnd-kit, pinned).

name: GlassLoadingSkeleton
target: Single GlassSkeleton primitive (shape bones) + GlassLoadingState (composition presets)
justification: This is one of three independent skeleton systems (GlassSkeleton, GlassSkeletonLoader, GlassLoadingSkeleton) with conflicting compound export names. It has the best a11y wiring of the three (role=status + reduced motion) but its shimmer and pulse classes do not exist in the stylesheet, and stacking backdrop blur on every bone is expensive for a placeholder. The certification screenshot shows bones at luminance >=229 on a 255 white canvas, i.e. effectively invisible grey-on-white. Keep its a11y contract and layout presets, fold into one skeleton API.

name: GlassLoadingState
target: Canonical loading-state composition; absorb skeleton presets from GlassLoadingSkeleton
justification: Best-structured file in the loading cluster: a small forwardRef wrapper over OptimizedGlass with no hard-coded material. But two of its three variants are broken because the utility classes they depend on (glass-animate-spin, glass-bg-primary) do not exist, and it has no test and no certification screenshot, so nothing caught it. Fix the class contract, add an accessible name to the progressbar, add reduced-motion-aware spin, and make this the single loading-state entry point.

name: GlassMetricChip
target: GlassChip / GlassBadge with a 'metric' slot layout (label, value, delta)
justification: A pill with three text spans; its only distinguishing props (intent, delta) produce no visual change, and it hard-overrides theme text tokens so it cannot follow dark mode. Screenshot shows a small grey pill with faint text on white (content band min luminance near 231 on mobile). The library already has GlassChip, GlassBadge and three dashboard stat cards; this belongs as a GlassChip layout, not a separate component.

name: GlassMetricsGrid
target: Compose from a single GlassStatCard + GlassSparkline inside a responsive grid layout primitive
justification: Kitchen-sink dashboard widget that re-implements stat card and sparkline instead of composing existing ones, ignores half its declared props, and has a keyboard-inoperable role=button. The screenshot shows only faint text with cards nearly invisible on a white canvas (component band saturation 0-2, card surfaces above luminance 225). A premium metrics surface needs real status color, tabular numerals, delta semantics and a composable card; rebuild on top of a consolidated stat card.

name: GlassNotificationCenter
target: One toast/notification system (GlassToastProvider + queue) with a notification-center list view
justification: Third independent toast/notification stack in the library (alongside data-display/GlassToast and feedback/GlassToast) with its own context, its own id generation and its own timers. Several advertised props do nothing, its overlay positioning depends on Tailwind classes the package does not ship, close controls are unlabeled, and Clear All is not a button. Merge into a single notifications engine; keep the 'center' as a list presentation over the same store.

name: CircularProgress
target: GlassProgressRing (own file, exported, with progressbar semantics)
justification: Internal, unexported and visibly broken (wrong start angle, colorless strokes, class names that are actually CSS values). Either rebuild as a proper exported ring or delete; a premium system needs a ring, so rebuild.

name: GlassProgress
target: GlassProgress (linear) with real intent tokens; split circular/steps into own files
justification: Progress is a core primitive, so it stays, but the current implementation has no working variants, no working stripes/indeterminate, and a leaked 'glass-radius-md' enum. The certification screenshot shows a light grey line on white (component band min luminance 240 on desktop), i.e. the fill is barely distinguishable. Rebuild around intent tokens, a proper indeterminate keyframe with reduced-motion fallback, and a liquid-glass track.

name: StepProgress
target: GlassWizard / stepper component
justification: Unexported, unstoried, inaccessible duplicate of the wizard step indicators that relies on a different design system's tokens. Delete and point to the canonical stepper.

name: GlassSchemaViewer
target: GlassJSONViewer
justification: A 32-line rename wrapper that inflates the component count without adding behavior and misleads by name. Deprecate in favour of GlassJSONViewer; if a real schema viewer is wanted, build it with property/type/required columns.

name: GlassSkeleton
target: Canonical GlassSkeleton (bone primitive) - keep this name, absorb the other two
justification: Has the right shape for the canonical bone primitive (forwardRef, shape variants, 8 stories) but ships a broken wave, double pulse, per-instance style injection, no reduced motion, and a leaked enum value. The certification crop shows only the story headings; the bones themselves sit above luminance 215 on white and do not register. Make this the single skeleton primitive with a CSS-defined shimmer, aria-hidden bones, and reduced-motion fallback; delete the other two implementations.

name: GlassSkeletonLoader
target: GlassLoadingState (spinner) + GlassSkeleton (bones)
justification: Misnamed spinner whose advertised variants are no-ops, whose compound helpers break reduced motion and depend on keyframes injected by a sibling, and whose exported names shadow the other skeleton implementations at the package root. It blocks server rendering of children. Nothing here is worth keeping beyond what GlassLoadingState and GlassSkeleton already cover.

name: GlassSparkline
justification: Small, deterministic, SSR-safe and genuinely useful; it should be the one sparkline that GlassMetricsGrid and stat cards compose. Needs a tokenized stroke, optional area gradient and endpoint dot, forwardRef, and an accessible name or aria-hidden contract. Screenshot shows a thin light line (band min luminance 202) - readable but not premium.

name: GlassStatusDot
target: GlassBadge dot variant or a tokenized GlassStatusIndicator
justification: The default status renders invisible outside Storybook because its color class is not shipped, and it has no non-color affordance or accessible label. A status dot is trivial to do right (intent tokens, optional pulse for busy with reduced-motion fallback, sr-only label); rebuild it as part of the badge/status family.

name: GlassTimeline
justification: Vertical mode is structurally sound (ul/li, responsive padding, min-width guards) and the screenshot shows three readable rows with title/subtitle/time, but cards are near-invisible on white (band min luminance ~200), horizontal mode depends on undefined Tailwind classes, and several advertised props are unimplemented. Worth polishing: tokenized card surface, working horizontal layout, wire onClick/disabled, delete the stub subcomponent.

name: GlassToast (+ GlassToastProvider, GlassToastViewport, useToast)
target: Single GlassToast system (merge data-display/GlassToast, feedback/GlassToast, GlassNotificationCenter)
justification: Toasts are a high-visibility surface and a natural Liquid Glass showcase, but this implementation does not float (positioning classes not shipped), dismisses at half the requested duration, runs two competing timers, announces nothing to assistive tech, and makes all types look identical. The feedback/ copy is the better-colored starting point (certification shows saturation 28 vs 0). Rebuild one toast engine with a proper queue, role=status/alert by type, reduced-motion, intent tokens and a real lensing material - then make it a flagship.

name: GlassToastProvider (re-export module)
target: GlassToast module
justification: Nine-line re-export. Keep the public symbol names but remove the file as a separately counted component once the toast system is unified.

name: GlassTreeView
target: One tree primitive (merge with tree-view/TreeView, back GlassFileTree and GlassTreeSelect)
justification: Two root-exported trees (GlassTreeView and TreeView) plus GlassFileTree and GlassTreeSelect each implement their own tree. This one looks like a card list rather than a tree, puts a backdrop-filter surface on every row, lacks WAI-ARIA tree keyboard support, and has broken uncontrolled single-select and nested check handling. Consolidate into one headless tree with roving focus and a flat row material; reuse it across file tree and tree select.

name: GlassVirtualTable
target: GlassDataTable (add a real virtualize option) / GlassDataGridPro
justification: A name that promises performance it does not deliver; consumers choosing it for large datasets will get full DOM rendering. Deprecate and add genuine windowing (e.g., virtualize prop backed by GlassVirtualList logic) to the canonical data table.

name: LiquidGlassBadgeCluster
target: Liquid Glass chip group (toggle group semantics) built on LiquidGlassMaterial
