justification: One of the few components on the real LiquidGlassMaterial/EffectGroup path, which is the right direction, but it disables every liquid effect, fakes selection, uses invalid ARIA and does nothing when uncontrolled. Rebuild as a proper chip/toggle group (role=group + buttons with aria-pressed, roving focus, uncontrolled expanded state) and let the material actually refract.

name: LiquidGlassCarouselRail
justification: Small, honest component that correctly uses the LiquidGlassScrollEdge primitive and is distinct enough from the full GlassCarousel (a rail, not a paged carousel) to keep. Needs GlassButton/LiquidGlass for the controls, 44px targets, reduced-motion-aware scrolling, end-state disabling, a focusable labelled scroller, and real tests and a certification screenshot.

name: Typography
category: typography / foundation (miscategorized under data-display; Storybook title 'Data + Visualization/Typography')
target: New foundation Text + Heading primitives (src/components/typography/) with as/asChild, separate level vs size, tone (primary/secondary/muted/inverse), weight, tracking, truncate/balance, a real tokenized type ramp (display/title/body/caption with line-height and letter-spacing), server-safe (no 'use client'); fold DisplayText and the CardTitle/DialogTitle/DrawerTitle/ChartTitle styles onto it; keep Typography as a deprecated alias.
justification: Typography is not exported from src/index.ts, so it is an internal helper used only by the cookie-consent components and GlassThemeDemo. It maps a variant name to a tag and adds a font-size class. It has no type ramp (line-height, weight, tracking, family), it ties visual scale to heading level, it has no tone or as-prop, and it marks itself 'use client' for no reason while importing ContrastGuard and motion modules it never uses. The story renders an empty element and the certification screenshot is a blank black/white page that still passed. A premium design system needs a strong first-party Text/Heading foundation that every title, card, and dialog shares. This component is not that, and its name blocks the right primitive from being built in its place. Replace it with a proper server-safe Text/Heading pair and keep this as a deprecated alias.

name: EnhancementShowcase
justification: This is a non-exported demo page that crashes under SSR (window in render), shows nothing to reduced-motion users, uses uncompilable dynamic classes, and makes unverifiable AI, emotion and biometric claims through hard-coded status labels. It is directly harmful to the premium positioning. Delete it, and let the LiquidGlassShowcase/docs site present only the components that actually ship.

name: GlassEcommerceProvider
target: move to examples/ or a separate demo package
justification: A design-system package should not ship a mock commerce backend: hard-coded tax, USD, random 'AI' recommendations, fake analytics, and state-mutating sort bugs, while not even exporting the hook needed to use it. Remove it from the library surface. If a commerce kit is needed, ship presentational, fully-controlled components and leave state to the app.

name: GlassProductRecommendations
target: if commerce is in scope: rebuild as presentational GlassProductCard + LiquidGlassCarouselRail
justification: It invents recommendation reasons and confidence percentages for caller-supplied data and presents them as AI output, which is a trust and legal liability for any adopter. It is also emoji-iconed, not keyboard accessible, and a fixed 4-column carousel on mobile. Remove it. A future commerce kit should be a controlled product card composed with the existing carousel rail.

name: GlassSmartShoppingCart
target: if commerce is in scope: rebuild as controlled GlassCartSummary + GlassQuantityStepper
justification: It hard-codes discount codes, tax, currency and a security claim into a UI library. Its controlled mode silently does nothing, its icon buttons are unlabeled, and it simulates network latency with setTimeout. None of this is salvageable as a design-system component. Remove it, and if needed provide a controlled cart summary and quantity stepper that hold no business logic.

name: GlassRichTextEditor
target: headless editor (Tiptap/Lexical) adapter wrapped in OptimizedGlass + shared LiquidGlassToolbar
justification: Writing the value prop straight into innerHTML with no sanitisation is a stored-XSS vector, and createLink accepts javascript: URLs from prompt(). It relies on deprecated execCommand, has no active-state feedback, and its placeholder overlaps typed text in uncontrolled mode. The glass shell is fine. Keep the visual wrapper and replace the engine with a maintained headless editor, using the library's LiquidGlassToolbar for the controls.

name: AuroraPro
target: marketing/AuroraBackground (CSS/GPU-cheap) as the single aurora
justification: This is a broken R3F demo hidden behind a version gate that can never succeed, so users get an empty div. Even unlocked, the shader would not compile because a React hook call is pasted into GLSL, the hooks usage violates React rules, and it leaks GPU resources. The story text even admits the fallback. Three other aurora components already exist; delete this one and the 'three' subpath entry.

name: Glass3DEngine
target: surfaces/GlassDepthLayer + a single useTilt hook
justification: Component-in-render remounting on every mousemove, around 650 blurred SVG nodes, conditional hooks, colliding filter ids and ungated tilt make this a performance and a11y liability. Its 'engine' claims (refraction, gaze, proximity) are not implemented. Pointer tilt and depth layering already exist elsewhere. Remove it and offer a single cheap useTilt hook and depth primitive.

name: GlassMorphingEngine
target: primitives/LiquidGlassMaterial (expose tunable CSS vars instead)
justification: It is a self-declared demo that, by default, ignores the context props it advertises, runs an ungated infinite shimmer, and ships Jest-detection branches in production code. The CSS-variable-driven spring pipeline is the only reusable idea, and that belongs in LiquidGlassMaterial as documented tunables, not in an 'environmental engine' with fake weather.

name: GlassPhysicsEngine
target: visual-feedback/RippleButton (press feedback) as the supported interaction effect
justification: A 60fps React-state particle loop with impure updaters, per-particle layout reads and an rAF restart on each render is not shippable, and cyan sparks with screen blending do not read as premium glass. Press-ripple feedback already exists in RippleButton. Remove it, or at most reimplement a single GPU-cheap press highlight inside the material primitive.

name: GlassShatterEffects
justification: Even if the dead version gate were fixed, the effect would crash on the first click (hook call outside render), render zero shards, and leave the wrapped content permanently invisible. Tests only assert that the fallback div renders. Shattering glass is also off-brand for a calm premium material system. Remove it along with the three subpath export.

name: SeasonalParticles
justification: This is novelty seasonal confetti that never renders, because the React version gate is unreachable. Its R3F implementation has unstable effect dependencies, side-effects in state updaters, broken seeding and GPU leaks. Three other particle components already exist. Remove it with the rest of the three subpath.

name: GlassMoodRing
justification: A novelty widget whose headline features (biometric, ambient) are random/clock fakes, whose default palette produces invalid CSS colors because hex alpha is appended to hsl(var()) strings, and which pulses indefinitely while ignoring OS reduced-motion by default. It has no plausible place in a premium first-party system; if a status ring is needed it should be rebuilt as a small token-driven indicator, not salvaged.

name: GlassToast (feedback)
target: src/components/data-display/GlassToastProvider.tsx
justification: Non-exported legacy duplicate of the shipped data-display toast system with a demo-harness as its main component, an unlabeled emoji close button, and a global keyframe collision. Nothing public depends on it; fold any useful bits (reduced-motion handling, position map) into the canonical GlassToastProvider and delete this file and its stories.

name: GlassErrorBoundary (components/)
target: src/utils/errorBoundary.tsx
justification: Same-named duplicate of the exported utils/errorBoundary GlassErrorBoundary. It adds an unconditional wrapper div, implicit gtag telemetry, a hard redirect to '/', and false 'our team will investigate' copy. Delete it and keep one canonical boundary, adding resetKeys and a configurable fallback there.

name: HoudiniGlassCard (+ HoudiniGlassShowcase)
target: GlassCard / LiquidGlassMaterial
justification: Sells CSS Houdini paint effects that are never registered, so the card is really a hard-coded rgba/blur card that depends on runtime-injected global CSS. It breaks hook rules, skips forwardRef and style passthrough, and its showcase is exported as public API. Deprecate it in favour of the canonical card on the shared material. Real Houdini enhancement, if wanted, belongs inside the material primitive, not a parallel card.

name: HoudiniGlassProvider (+ useHoudiniGlass, useGlassEffect, glassPresets)
target: LiquidGlassLayerProvider / ThemeProvider tokens
justification: This is a mock of CSS Houdini. Its worklets are never loaded, its property registrations use invalid var() initial values, and it overwrites global design tokens on <html> with no cleanup. That is hostile to a token-driven system and unsafe when two instances mount. Remove it along with HoudiniGlassCard. If progressive Houdini enhancement is ever wanted, build it inside the canonical material primitive with real worklet modules.

name: ClearIcon
target: src/icons (XIcon/CloseIcon)
justification: Internal one-off X icon duplicating the icon package, with a clickable-SVG anti-pattern and conflicting prop types. Replace its two uses in GlassMultiSelect with the canonical XIcon (aria-hidden), then delete the file, its story and its test.

name: ImageList (+ GlassImageList)
justification: Small and token-correct, and a reasonable media grid primitive. It needs a direct ref, removal of the dead animation props and the 'galileo' class, real or removed quilted/woven variants, and a decision on whether masonry lives here or in GlassMasonryGrid; consolidate the masonry implementations into one. The material approach (CSS module plus aura tokens) is the pattern other components should copy.

name: ImageListItem (+ GlassImageListItem)
justification: The material and motion are sound. The API and ARIA are buggy: rest props are spread twice and leak to the DOM, role=button on an li breaks list semantics, aria-expanded is misused on hover, and intent/tier are dead props. Fix it by rendering an inner <button> for interactive items, keeping the li semantic, spreading rest props once, and deleting the dead props.

name: ImageListItemBar (+ GlassImageListItemBar)
justification: Simple and close to acceptable. Swap the hard-coded black text for an on-glass text token so it works in dark themes, reveal on :focus-within as well as hover, accept ReactNode titles, and render as a figcaption. Keep it as part of the ImageList family.

name: GlassImageProcessingProvider (ImageProcessingProvider)
justification: This 1.4k-line mock 'AI image service' fakes analysis, face detection, optimization and cloud upload with Math.random and setTimeout. It returns example.com URLs and corrupts blob URLs, and its context hook isn't even exported. Shipping it in a design system is a liability: it implies capabilities that do not exist. Remove it from the package, or at most move it to a demo/examples workspace.

name: GlassIntelligentImageUploader
target: src/components/input/GlassFileUpload.tsx
justification: A demo uploader that fronts a fake AI backend. It has at least five dead buttons, filters that don't affect the preview, a modal without dialog semantics or focus management, and uploads that vanish without the unexported provider. Remove it with the provider. If a premium image dropzone is needed, extend GlassFileUpload with real preview, accessible drop target and progress.

name: Glass360Viewer
justification: The name promises a 360° panorama viewer. The implementation crops a rectangle of a flat image onto an unsized 300x150 canvas: zoom, projections, VR and quality are no-ops, and hotspots render black because canvas ignores CSS variables. A correct viewer needs WebGL spherical projection, which is out of scope for a glass design system and is better left to dedicated libraries. Remove it. At most, offer a glass controls overlay that wraps a third-party viewer.

name: GlassARPreview
justification: A fake AR component. There is no XR session, tracking is random, renderObject and the lighting props are dead, and canvas colors are invalid. In camera mode a dependency bug loops getUserMedia, which is a privacy and battery hazard. It cannot be polished into a real AR feature inside a design system. Remove it from the public API.

name: GlassFluidSimulation
justification: A toy O(n^2) particle demo branded as an SPH fluid simulation. Trails are broken by in-place mutation, the preset, debug and trails controls are no-ops, it uses a fixed 800px canvas, re-subscribes rAF every frame, and draws nothing under reduced motion. It is not a design-system component. Remove it. If ambient liquid motion is wanted, it belongs in one consolidated, GPU-backed background effect.

name: GlassHologram
justification: A sci-fi decoration with severe correctness bugs. Interaction is unwired (detached containerRef), layers cannot be selected (pointer-events none), positions re-randomize every frame, half the color schemes emit invalid CSS, and the whole tree re-renders at 60fps. It carries generic global keyframe names and does nothing a premium glass system needs. Remove it.

name: GlassParticleField
target: backgrounds/ParticleBackground (single ambient particle effect)
justification: The least broken of the immersive canvases: colors are sanitized and there is a reduced-motion static seed. It is still one of five or more overlapping particle systems, with dead feature props, hard-coded white fill, setState-per-frame rendering and no DPR handling. Merge its good ideas (deterministic seed, color sanitizer) into one ambient particle background that keeps state in refs, is DPR-aware, sits behind content as aria-hidden, and reads OS reduced motion. Then delete this one.

name: GlassVortexPortal
justification: Its control panel is mostly inert: type, color and three toggles are empty onChange handlers. The core animation decays itself to nothing through per-frame opacity multiplication, and the canvas darkens to black over the light gradient. Thirteen stories and a 'certified' screenshot mask a component that does not work as named. Remove it.

name: GlassCheckbox
justification: A checkbox you can't click and whose checked state has no fill doesn't meet the bar. Rebuild it as a native input inside a <label> with a peer-styled glass box, using real token-driven checked/indeterminate fills, a defined :focus-visible ring and a native indeterminate property, and drop the dead OptimizedGlass props. Every group, tree and table should then compose this one primitive.

name: GlassCheckboxGroup
target: GlassCheckbox (group = fieldset + legend composing GlassCheckbox)
justification: This is a second checkbox implementation with different markup, focus model and visuals from GlassCheckbox, and it nests two glass layers per row. Replace it with a thin fieldset/legend group that composes the redesigned GlassCheckbox. Keep the min/max and option-card ideas, and remove the dead standalone path and the sound effects.

name: GlassColorPicker
justification: A premium picker needs a 2D saturation/value plane, a hue strip, an alpha checkerboard, an eyedropper where available, and real popover behavior (portal, positioning, focus trap, Escape). The current version has duplicate global IDs, a Cancel that doesn't cancel, and ignores defaultValue for its initial slider state. Rebuild it on primitives/positioning and primitives/focus, and share swatch and gradient-stop pieces with GlassGradientPicker.

name: GlassCombobox
target: Unified GlassCombobox/GlassSelect family (single + multi) on the GlassMultiSelect engine + primitives/positioning + dismissable-layer
justification: Small and fairly correct, but it's one of at least six select/combobox implementations. Keep its ARIA pattern (input-as-combobox with activedescendant) as the reference model for a single unified Select/Combobox that supports single/multi selection, groups, async, creatable and a portal popover. Fix blur-dismiss before retiring it.

name: GlassDateField
justification: An honest thin wrapper over the native date control. It's the right fallback for mobile and for low-JS forms. It improves automatically once GlassInput is redesigned. Hide the native picker indicator or drop the leftIcon to avoid the doubled glyph.

name: GlassDatePicker
target: Single GlassDatePicker (single|range|multiple) over one shared GlassCalendar grid
justification: Date pickers are a showcase surface for a premium system, but this one has no grid keyboard model, fake week numbers, an ignored format prop, a 201-option native select, and 42 heavyweight GlassButtons per month. Build one calendar grid (role=grid, roving focus, locale weekdays, ISO week numbers) shared with GlassCalendar, and use it for single, range and presets. Put it in a positioned, portal popover with a focus trap.

name: GlassDateRangePicker
target: GlassDatePicker (mode='range' with presets slot)
justification: Its core job, picking a range by clicking two dates, is broken by the selection logic, and the trigger can't be reached by keyboard. The test suite only smoke-renders, so the defect shipped. Fold presets and the dual-month layout into the redesigned GlassDatePicker range mode, then deprecate this export.

name: GlassFieldGroup
justification: Simple and semantically right. Swap the hard-coded white alpha for a surface token that works in light and dark, link the description to the group, and make it the standard group wrapper used by the checkbox and radio groups.

name: GlassFileUpload (input/)
target: src/components/interactive/GlassFileUpload.tsx (the root export)
justification: This file isn't reachable from the package: root exports interactive/GlassFileUpload, and input/index.ts doesn't export it. It's an orphan with its own story, test and certification screenshot, which inflates counts. It uses alert(), emoji icons and colliding IDs. Delete it and fold anything unique (the XHR progress path) into the exported upload component.

name: GlassForm (+ GlassFormItem/Label/Control/Description/Message, useFormField)
target: Merge with GlassFormField.tsx into one forms module exported under the ./forms subpath
justification: The RHF binding pattern is sound, but the public surface is broken: consumers get a bare FormProvider and a different GlassFormField with the same name. Rework it into a single forms API: Form, FormField (Controller), FormItem (layout, absorbing GlassFormField.tsx), FormLabel, FormControl, FormMessage. Export all of it from root or ./forms, and use semantic message tokens instead of Tailwind palette names.

name: GlassFormField
target: GlassForm (FormItem + Slot-based FormControl)
justification: This is the same concept as GlassForm's item/label/message but without control wiring, so the label and error aren't associated unless the caller does it manually. Merge it into the forms module, where the Slot-based control gets the ID and describedby automatically, and resolve the export-name collision.

name: GlassFormStepper (+ GlassCompactStepper)
target: GlassStepper (single stepper primitive used by GlassWizard)
justification: It's at least the fifth stepper in the library and uses two styling dialects internally. Fold its useful bits (error/optional states, compact mode) into one GlassStepper that GlassWizard and form templates consume, then deprecate this export.

name: GlassFormTable
target: GlassDataGrid editable-cell mode
justification: This is a minimal repeatable-rows widget with string-only cells and index keys, which isn't premium and overlaps with three table/grid components. Deprecate it in favor of an editable-cell mode on GlassDataGrid, or a FieldArray recipe in the forms module.

name: GlassInput
justification: GlassInput is the foundation of every form, picker and search field, and it's the most important component in this shard. Several of its documented props don't work: variants and state borders are masked by inline styles, a custom id breaks the label, and a custom onFocus kills the focus state. Rebuild it as a token-driven field (surface, border, focus, and state tokens through CSS variables) with no inline material, no hover lift, a slot-based adornment API, a correct describedby, and lazy liquid material. Then GlassDateField, GlassTimeField and GlassSearchField become trivial.

name: GlassLabel
justification: A label should be a trivial, rock-solid typographic primitive. This one ships undefined, theme-inverted colors and an extra div wrapper. Switch to semantic text tokens, drop the wrapper (or make it optional), and make every control in the library use it instead of six bespoke label snippets.

name: GlassMultiSelect
target: Becomes engine of unified Select/Combobox family
justification: It has the best engineering foundation here: token-based CSS module, real interaction tests, and a complete feature set. It needs proper combobox ARIA (input role=combobox, activedescendant, option IDs), a positioned/portal popover with a blur-consistent material and an entry transition, sm/md/lg naming, and closeOnSelect=false by default. After that it should absorb GlassCombobox, GlassSelect and GlassSelectCompound as single/multi modes.

name: GlassMultiStepForm (+ GlassFormStep, useFormContext)
target: GlassWizard
justification: This is one of four or more wizard and multi-step implementations, with skippable validation, misleading 'Data Saved' UI, and export names that collide with react-hook-form and GlassFormStepper. Merge its async step validation into GlassWizard, built on the unified stepper and forms module, and retire this export.

name: GlassRadioGroup (+ GlassRadioGroupItem, useRadioGroup)
justification: A radio group without arrow keys or native form participation is a correctness failure, not a polish issue. Rebuild it on native radio inputs (or primitives/roving-focus) inside a fieldset, with token-driven selected surfaces for both themes. Share the option-card layout with the redesigned checkbox group, and remove the dead context and announce calls.

name: GlassSearchField
target: LiquidGlassSearchField (single search field), or make it a documented preset of GlassInput
justification: This is a reasonable 60-line preset, but the library ships two root-exported search fields (GlassSearchField and LiquidGlassSearchField) plus GlassIntelligentSearch. The clear button only works when the field is controlled and onClear is passed, and the role is redundant. Keep one search field as the canonical one. Implement clear internally for uncontrolled usage, add Escape-to-clear, and forward clearable correctly. No certification screenshot exists for it.

name: GlassSelect (legacy, options-array)
target: GlassSelectCompound (after it is rebuilt on a real listbox/combobox primitive)
justification: The legacy select is already self-declared deprecated, yet it holds the root `GlassSelect` name. It has broken focus semantics (a duplicate hidden select), mouse selection likely broken by its outside-click handler, controlled-only state, dead variant/state maps, and text-glyph chevrons. Tests never open it. It should become a thin adapter over the compound select, with options mapped to Item children, for one major version, and then be removed. The certification screenshot could not be visually inspected in this run (the image reader returned nothing). Certification marked it 'passed' after inspecting only the storybook-default-dark theme.

name: GlassSelectCompound (GlassSelectRoot/Trigger/Content/Item/Value/Label/Group/Separator/ScrollUp/ScrollDown)
target: Canonical AuraGlass 5 Select built on primitives/roving-focus + positioning, with a shared Liquid material listbox surface
justification: The compound API is the right shape and is the obvious foundation for the single 5.0 select. The internals are not production grade: no in-list keyboard navigation, an anchor-dismiss toggle bug, a hard-coded aria-label, dead scroll buttons, and dead Tailwind animation classes. Its material does not use the library's own glass primitive. A premium select is a flagship surface in any glass system (Apple's pop-up menus are its most recognisable 'material' moment). Rebuild it on RovingFocusGroup/Positioner, render content through LiquidGlassMaterial, and make it the only select with legacy GlassSelect as an adapter. Screenshot not viewable in this run.

name: GlassSlider
justification: A Liquid Glass slider (a refractive thumb that magnifies the track) is one of the most recognisable Liquid Glass controls and is flagship material. The current one fails basic WCAG because there is no keyboard operation at all. It also violates hook rules, commits stale values, floods the live region, and advertises four inert props. Rebuild it on pointer capture with keyboard support (step/page/home/end), aria-orientation and a single debounced announcement. Use a real LiquidGlassMaterial thumb and token-driven fill, and drop the fake props. Screenshot not viewable in this run.

name: GlassStep
target: single Stepper/Steps component (interactive/GlassStepper) with Step as a composable child
justification: This is an internal step cell that nothing in the library composes, yet it is root-exported alongside its own icon and label sub-pieces. The library already has at least five other step-indicator implementations. Fold it into one Steps component (Steps.Root/Steps.Item) with a single shared material rail rather than per-step glass slabs, and stop exporting it standalone.

name: GlassStepIcon
target: internal part of consolidated Steps component
justification: This is a decorative sub-part with no consumer outside GlassStep. Its state colours depend on Tailwind classes that do not exist here, so active and completed states are visually indistinguishable unless the consumer runs Tailwind with the library in its content paths. It should not be public API.

name: GlassStepLabel
target: internal part of consolidated Steps component
justification: This is a span with theme-breaking hard-coded slate colours (undefined in this repo), identical completed and default states, and three ignored glass props. It has no consumer besides GlassStep. Remove it from the public surface.

name: GlassStepper (input; numeric spin button)
target: new GlassNumberField (built on GlassInput + spinbutton semantics)
justification: It is not exported anywhere, so it is effectively dead code with a misleading name that collides with the public progress GlassStepper. The behaviour has concrete bugs: double increments on touch, a long-press that does not accumulate, dropped props, duplicate ids, and hook-rule violations. It also plays sounds by default. Replace it with a properly named NumberField that reuses GlassInput, and delete this file.

name: GlassSwitch
justification: The Liquid Glass switch (an elongating lens thumb on a tinted track) is a signature control, and this one has a sound semantic base (a real button with role=switch). Visually it cannot express state. Track variant colours are never applied, the tint is discarded by the primitive, the thumb fill may be undefined when off, and the thumb is mis-centred with asymmetric travel. Rebuild the visuals on tokens: a tinted track fill, a centred thumb computed from padding, an RTL-aware logical transform and reduced-motion gating. Use LiquidGlassMaterial for the thumb. Keep the API.

name: GlassTextarea
justification: The core is acceptable and visually consistent, because the CSS override unifies everything. But the variant and state API is fake, error semantics are broken (dangling describedby, error not coloured or announced), auto-resize and char count ignore uncontrolled usage, and icons overlap. Fix these against GlassInput's field contract, preferably by sharing a FieldShell for label/helper/error. Remove the dead variants or make them real through tokens.

name: GlassTimeField
justification: This is a correct, tiny preset over GlassInput with native semantics. Polish later by styling the native ::-webkit-calendar-picker-indicator for glass themes, and add a test. No certification screenshot exists.

name: GlassToggle (+ non-exported GlassToggleGroup, GlassToggleGroupItem, useToggle, useToggleGroup)
target: src/components/toggle-button/ToggleButton + ToggleButtonGroup (rebuilt on a real <button> + RovingFocusGroup), rendered inside LiquidGlassControlGroup
justification: This toggle is not keyboard accessible: a div role=button with no tabIndex or key handling. Its group variant is functionally dead because `value` is dropped, and its pressed styling depends on non-existent classes. A separate toggle-button family already exists. Merge into one ToggleButton/ToggleButtonGroup on a native button with roving focus, and remove GlassToggle (or alias it) in 5.0.

name: GlassTransferList
target: GlassMultiSelect (or a later rebuilt pattern in a workflows recipe)
justification: It is not exported anywhere, so it is dead to consumers. Transfer lists are an outdated enterprise pattern that conflicts with a premium glass aesthetic. The implementation loses keyboard focus on every move, has unlabeled search fields and unlabeled lists, and is controlled-only. Remove it from the component set. If needed later, rebuild it as a documented recipe composed from GlassCheckboxGroup and GlassSearchField.

name: GlassTreeSelect
target: compose canonical Select popover + tree-view/TreeView (role=tree) as a TreeSelect recipe
justification: It is unexported and lacks tree ARIA. It nests interactive elements, mutates state during render, is not portalled, and hard-codes blue. The library already has three tree implementations, one of them (tree-view/TreeView) with proper role=tree. Rebuild TreeSelect as a composition of the canonical Select popover and TreeView rather than maintaining a fourth tree.

name: GlassValidationMessage
justification: This is the right primitive and should become the single message renderer used by every field, instead of each field duplicating error markup. Replace the undefined Tailwind tone classes with semantic tokens (--glass-status-danger-fg, etc.) that meet contrast on all themes. Add a visually hidden tone prefix, and drop the glass slab by default (inline text plus icon), keeping it as an opt-in variant. No certification screenshot exists.

name: GlassWizard (+ non-exported GlassWizardStep, GlassWizardStepper, useWizard)
target: one Wizard/MultiStepForm in the ./workflows subpath, using the consolidated Steps component
justification: At least five overlapping multi-step implementations exist (GlassWizard, GlassMultiStepForm, GlassFormStepper, GlassWizardTemplate, GlassFormWizardSteps). This one composes real primitives, but its state is undermined by undefined classes. It permits skipping validation through the step nav, has a frozen controlled mode in its own stories, ships an inconsistent useWizard fallback, and has a no-op GlassWizardStep. Pick one wizard and give it step-scoped data/validation via render props or context. Move focus on step change, use token-driven step states and the shared Steps component.

name: LiquidGlassControlGroup
justification: This is the one component in the shard that uses the intended Liquid material stack (LiquidGlassMaterial + LiquidGlassEffectGroup), and a segmented/toolbar control group is a core Liquid Glass flagship (merged lenses). But its behavioural props are fakes. Wire RovingFocusGroup, role=toolbar/radiogroup by selectionMode, aria-orientation and managed pressed/checked state, and make density real. Move the story's !important look into the component, then make it the base for ToggleButtonGroup and segmented controls. No certification screenshot exists.

name: ContextAwareGlass
target: OptimizedGlass / GlassCard (adaptive contrast belongs in the material primitive)
justification: Not exported from root, duplicates advanced/GlassContextAware, and its core promise is hollow: the adaptation math feeds an `intensity` prop the primitive throws away, so the only output is a choice among 4 elevation classes. The certified screenshot has no ink at all (darkest pixel 228/255): it is an empty pale rectangle on a near-white gradient. If background-adaptive legibility is wanted for 5.0 it should be a real luminance-sampling capability inside the material primitive, not a wrapper.

name: CursorGlow
target: A single pointer-light/specular-highlight primitive in the material system (OptimizedGlass cursorHighlight / LiquidGlass specular)
justification: A pointer-following specular highlight is a legitimate premium-glass ingredient, but this implementation is a full-viewport screen-blended blob, is broken with its own default color, mispositions in local mode, and leaks props to the DOM. It is not root-exported. Fold the idea into the material primitive as a per-surface specular response (local coordinates, token colors, reduced-motion aware) and delete this file.

name: GlassA11yAuditor
target: Docs/devtools package backed by axe-core, not the design-system runtime bundle
justification: A homemade accessibility linter shipped inside a UI kit is a liability: its heuristics produce false positives/negatives, it audits the whole document regardless of children, and it is itself mis-roled (role=application). This is not a visual component a premium design system needs; if kept at all it belongs in a Storybook addon powered by axe-core.

name: GlassAdvancedSearch
target: LiquidGlassSearchField + a composable SearchCombobox/FilterBar (GlassFilterBar) recipe
justification: One of at least six search surfaces. Most of its advertised features are broken or unwired (debounce, sort, view mode, saved searches, three of six filter types) and the suggestion list lacks combobox semantics. The certification capture shows only the card header region (ink bbox 254x74px) on a near-white page - nothing premium. Keep one search field primitive and a documented composition pattern; delete this monolith.

name: GlassAvatarGroup
target: src/components/data-display/GlassAvatar.tsx GlassAvatarGroup (single Avatar + AvatarGroup family)
justification: Functional and reasonably accessible, but it is the second GlassAvatarGroup in the codebase and hard-codes dark-theme white text/borders over the glass mixin. Certified capture shows a tiny 119x23px ink cluster on a pale page. Merge into the data-display Avatar family, render via the Avatar component (so images/fallbacks/status are shared), and use tokens for ring/status colors.

name: GlassCardLink (interactive)
target: GlassCard (interactive + asChild/href) or card/glass-card-link.tsx
justification: This file is not what consumers get: src/index.ts:271 exports a different 38-line GlassCardLink from components/card. Having two same-named components with incompatible APIs is a pure maintenance hazard. Its variant system is a no-op because the primitive discards intensity/tint. Replace with a linkable GlassCard (asChild) and delete.

name: GlassCarousel
target: LiquidGlassCarouselRail rebuilt as a proper APG carousel (scroll-snap, controlled index, scoped keyboard, reduced-motion autoplay pause)
justification: The carousel hijacks global keyboard input, has unlabeled controls, breaks Rules of Hooks, and drags in a pseudo-AI 'consciousness' stack whose eye-tracking is literally commented out. The certification screenshot certified the empty state ('No items to display', ink bbox 117x13px) because the Default story passes no items. A carousel is a likely showcase surface in 5.0, so it needs a ground-up rewrite on scroll-snap with real a11y rather than polishing this.

name: GlassChat
target: Composable Chat primitives: ChatLog(role=log) + MessageBubble + GlassChatInput composer; drop consciousness features
justification: Chat is a high-value surface for an AI-era glass system, but this is a 1,245-line monolith where half the code is simulated intelligence and many visible controls do nothing. Bubbles are flat Tailwind, not the material system. Rebuild as small composable parts (log, bubble, composer, typing indicator) with real ARIA log semantics and token-driven bubble materials.

name: GlassChatInput
target: Single GlassChatComposer used by the Chat family (controlled value, IME-safe Enter handling, real MediaRecorder or no voice)
justification: A composer is worth having, but this one ships a broken primary interaction (Enter never sends because of a stale closure), ID collisions, and a mock audio blob handed to the consumer. It should become the one composer for GlassChat with a controlled API, onKeyDown + isComposing handling, and either genuine MediaRecorder support or no voice feature.

name: GlassCoachmarks
target: GlassTour built on primitives/positioning + dismissable-layer + focus scope with spotlight cutout
justification: Small and cheap, but it does not do what coachmarks do (anchor to and spotlight a target) and fails basic dialog accessibility. The capture shows a full-width bottom bar (ink bbox 1359x80px) over the story's own mock dashboard. A real tour component built on the existing positioning/dismissable-layer/focus primitives would be a credible premium feature.

name: GlassCodeEditor
target: GlassCodeSurface: themed chrome around CodeMirror 6 (lazy-loaded) or a read-only Shiki code block
justification: Advertises syntax highlighting, minimap and themes but delivers a transparent textarea over plain text with a non-scrolling gutter and an unescaped placeholder sink. The capture is a cramped 268x104px ink region. A design system should supply glass chrome and tokens for a real editor engine, not reimplement one badly.

name: GlassColorSchemeGenerator
target: Docs-site theme playground (not runtime library)
justification: A naive HSL palette generator is docs tooling, not a UI component customers ship. It exports non-portable var() strings and has no contrast validation, which is the one thing a design-system palette tool must do. Move to the docs site or a separate devtools package.

name: GlassColorWheel
target: src/components/input/GlassColorPicker.tsx (rebuild on accessible 2D slider + hue slider primitives)
justification: Not exported, duplicates GlassColorPicker, and is completely inaccessible to keyboard and touch. Canvas fillStyle with CSS vars and var() swatches are outright bugs. Fold any useful conversion utilities into the main picker and delete.

name: GlassCommand
target: One cmdk-style GlassCommand (Command/Input/List/Group/Item compound, combobox ARIA) that GlassCommandPalette and LiquidGlassCommandSurface become thin shells of
justification: Command menus are a signature premium surface (Raycast/Linear/Apple Spotlight), so the concept is flagship-worthy, but the library has five overlapping command components and this one lacks listbox/combobox semantics. Make this the single compound headless+glass command primitive (borrowing the compound structure already sketched here) and delete the rest. Capture shows a modest 262x304px card with legible ink.

name: GlassCommandPalette
target: Unified GlassCommand compound primitive (palette = dialog shell around it)
justification: The most complete command surface here (dialog semantics, listbox, shortcuts, footer hints) and the capture is the richest in the shard (edge density 3.3%, full-width overlay). But the regex crash on common characters and dead recents are release-blocking, and it duplicates four sibling command components. Merge its features into one command primitive with combobox ARIA, an escaped/scored matcher, and recents stored by id.

name: GlassCommentThread
target: src/components/collaboration/GlassCollaborativeComments.tsx (or a single CommentThread built on Avatar + Composer)
justification: Simple and honest, but visually a stack of identical pale boxes with an input under every comment, and it overlaps the larger collaboration comments component. Merge into one comment-thread component that reuses Avatar and the chat composer, with list semantics and reply-on-demand.

name: GlassComponentPlayground
target: Docs site / Storybook controls
justification: A component playground is documentation infrastructure; shipping it in the runtime package bloats the API and it hand-rolls tabs and buttons with inline rgba instead of using the library's own components - the opposite of dogfooding. Move to the docs app.

name: GlassDraggable
target: dnd-kit-based GlassSortable/Draggable recipes (keyboard sensor, pointer sensor, announcements) with a glass 'lifted' material state
justification: The headline component is non-functional due to stale closures, the droppable throws on dragover, and the pieces use incompatible event models. It has no glass material and zero accessibility. Rebuild on dnd-kit (or a pointer-events + keyboard sensor implementation) and contribute only the visual lifted/drop-target states from the design system.

name: GlassDrawingCanvas
justification: Not exported from the root, so it is not part of the public API. Half of its advertised tools are fake (shape and text tools just draw freehand). Toolbar icons are letters and emoji. The canvas is a fixed-pixel (800x600) opaque white rectangle that breaks mobile layouts, and the SVG export is mislabelled. Making it real (shape tools, vector export, a responsive DPR-aware canvas, keyboard access) is a product in itself and out of scope for a glass design system. Keep it as an internal demo or remove it.

name: GlassFacetSearch
target: GlassSearch (combobox) + GlassFilterPanel (single facet engine)
justification: This duplicates GlassFilterPanel's facet rendering almost line for line, and other parts of the library already provide search. The reduced-motion pattern hides content, results are mouse-only, the debounce leaks timers, and single-select facets use checkboxes. Rebuild it as a composition: a proper ARIA combobox search field, a shared facet engine for filters, and a results list. It should not remain a standalone 675-line monolith.

name: GlassFileExplorer
justification: The concept is valid for an app-grade glass system, but the implementation is a facade. The context menu is a stub, rename and delete can't be reached, the rows have no keyboard model, and the dialog is not a dialog. The material is defined three times with inline rgba overriding the elevation API. Rebuild it on a shared FileItem model with the library's Menu, Dialog, and roving-tabindex grid, and share the icon and size utilities with GlassFileTree.

name: GlassFileTree
target: GlassTreeView (single WAI-ARIA tree with file-icon renderer preset)
justification: This is the third tree implementation in the library. It is inaccessible (no tree roles or arrow keys) and has an architectural bug: a component defined in render, which remounts the subtree on every render. Several allow* flags do nothing, and expansion is invisible under reduced motion. Fold its file-icon and size display into a single accessible GlassTreeView as a renderer preset, then delete this file.

name: GlassFileUpload
target: single GlassFileUpload / Dropzone (merge with src/components/input/GlassFileUpload.tsx)
justification: File upload is a core component every product needs, and this one uses the right primitive. But two components share the same name, the progress bar is fake, batch upload has a race condition, and the dropzone can't be operated from the keyboard. Merge both into one Dropzone with real progress callbacks (onUpload(file, {onProgress})), object-URL previews, aria-live errors, and key handling. It can then be a solid KEEP-tier component.

name: GlassFilterBar
justification: This is the most honest component in the shard: small, typed, forwardRef, with no fake features. It needs to compose the system's chip/tag component (with a proper dismiss icon and 24 px+ targets), adopt the shared glass surface primitive instead of a flat bg-white/8, and gain a test and a visual certification target. Positioned as the 'active filters' row that pairs with GlassFilterPanel.

name: GlassFilterPanel
target: canonical facet/filter engine absorbing GlassFacetSearch facets
justification: This is the better of the two facet implementations and should become the canonical one. It needs a single material source (drop the inline rgba overrides), proper disclosure semantics, the library Dialog for presets, and removal of the compact-mode group truncation, which exists only to make screenshots fit. Paired with GlassFilterBar it forms a coherent filtering family.

name: GlassFocusRing
target: token-driven :focus-visible ring in the base glass styles + optional asChild FocusRing Slot
justification: A focus-ring wrapper that adds an extra tab stop and can hide its children from assistive technology makes accessibility worse. Three focus-indicator components exist. The premium answer is one token-driven :focus-visible ring baked into every interactive primitive (outline plus specular halo that works on glass), optionally exposed as an asChild Slot. Replace this component and its siblings with that.

name: GlassFormBuilder
target: GlassForm + GlassFormField (schema renderer as a thin helper)
justification: This is one of at least seven form or wizard implementations. The 'wizard' variant is fake, the file type renders nothing, the controlled API is broken, autosave triggers submit, and layout depends on a Storybook utility shim. Keep at most a thin schema-to-GlassFormField renderer layered on the canonical GlassForm, then remove the rest.

name: GlassGallery
justification: A glass media gallery could be a showcase, but this one has dead responsive and aspect classes, so the 'grid' isn't really a grid. Masonry is fake, Like and Share do nothing, the lightbox opens the wrong image after filtering and shows duplicate navigation, and the list layout is broken. Rebuild it on prefixed tokens and CSS grid with a real Dialog-based lightbox, composing GlassLazyImage tiles. ImageList should either merge in or be removed.

name: GlassGestureZone
justification: Not exported publicly. Its controls are dead, its gesture recognition is cosmetic (tap and double-tap are the same template, and 'pinch' is a line), and it burns CPU with an always-on rAF loop plus two 60 Hz setState intervals. Fixed pixel sizes break mobile. It duplicates MultiDimensionalGestureRecognizer. Nothing here belongs in a premium design system. If gesture support is needed, expose a headless usePointerGesture hook built on the existing gesturePhysics.

name: GlassGradientPicker
justification: A gradient picker is useful for theme tooling, but this one cannot be controlled, doesn't emit changes for most edits, emits stale values otherwise, renders broken preset swatches, and uses inverted icon semantics. Rebuild it on GlassColorPicker with a draggable stop track, a controlled value of {type, angle, stops}, and a deterministic CSS serializer, or drop it from the core package.

name: GlassImageViewer
justification: The feature set is real and close to useful. The main blockers are fixable: the page-wide keyboard hijack (scope it to a focused container), dead unprefixed layout classes, the left-1/2 typo, the passive-wheel preventDefault, pointer events for touch pan and pinch, and Dialog-based fullscreen. After that it should become the single lightbox engine for GlassGallery.

name: GlassInfiniteScroll
justification: A small, mostly honest utility. Needed changes: forwardRef, a root option (container or viewport), proper feed/aria-busy/aria-live semantics, removal of the mirrored state, prefixed classes, and a fix for the reverse-mode sentinel. It is low risk and worth keeping, but it is plumbing, not a visual showcase.

name: GlassInlineEdit
justification: The behaviour is right and the component is small. It should compose GlassInput, accept a label, disabled, validate, and save-on-blur, use forwardRef, and return focus to the trigger after commit or cancel. It then becomes the shared inline-rename primitive that FileTree and FileExplorer reuse instead of hand-rolling.

name: GlassKanban
target: GlassKanbanBoard (after its own audit)
justification: A Kanban without drag and drop, with conditional hooks that crash when props change, disabled 'eye tracking', mock-event 'consciousness' recording, and a window global for audio. It is the textbook fake-complexity component. A second Kanban (GlassKanbanBoard) already exists. Delete this one and its six 'Consciousness' variants, and invest in a single accessible board built on dnd-kit-style keyboard DnD.

name: GlassKeyValueEditor
justification: An honest, small, controlled component that is useful in dev-tool and settings UIs. It should compose GlassInput and icon buttons, use stable row IDs, add duplicate-key validation, forwardRef, and a disabled state, and sit on a proper glass surface. That is low effort.

name: GlassLazyImage
target: GlassImage (single image primitive: native lazy + blur-up + optional overlay slot)
justification: Blur-up lazy images are a legitimate primitive, but this one bundles a hover-only, unlabelled action menu with a stub zoom, and it never renders the img during SSR. It doesn't pass through img attributes and relies on unprefixed classes. Split it into a lean GlassImage (native loading and srcSet passthrough, blur-up placeholder, an aspect-ratio token) with composable overlays. The actions belong to the gallery or card, not the image.

name: GlassMentionList
target: GlassCombobox / a shared Listbox primitive (role=listbox + roving focus) exposed as a MentionMenu recipe
justification: A 60-line styled <ul> of buttons is not a mention component: no listbox semantics, no keyboard model, no anchoring to the caret. The library already has listbox-like components (Combobox, CommandPalette). Fold it into a shared Listbox primitive and ship mention as a documented recipe on that primitive rather than a separate root export.

name: GlassMessageList
target: Merge with GlassChat into a single chat kit (MessageList + MessageBubble + Composer) built on GlassVirtualList
justification: Chat is a legitimate premium showcase surface, but this implementation is a hover-only, mouse-only list with dead props (virtualScroll), fake read receipts, raw Tailwind status colours and page-scrolling auto-scroll. It overlaps GlassChat. Redesign as one chat kit with real bubble styling, keyboard-reachable actions, a true status model and virtualization.

name: GlassMindMap (+ useMindMap)
target: Remove from root; if a diagram surface is wanted, rebuild on a real graph lib (React Flow) adapter with glass node skins
justification: The interactive features it advertises (drag, add/delete, minimap) are broken or unwired, it is mouse-only with zero keyboard access, and its palette is hard-coded dark rgba. The certification screenshot shows a small cluster of nodes in a mostly empty pale frame. Building a correct mind-map is a product in itself; deprecate and point to a glass-skinned adapter over an established graph engine.

name: GlassPatternBuilder
justification: Not exported from any entry point, so it is dead weight with nine stories advertising it. It renders a black canvas due to CSS-var-in-canvas bugs, leaks compounding rAF loops, has a stubbed drag path, a fixed 800px canvas and is outside a design system's remit. Delete it and its stories/tests/snapshots.

name: GlassPresets (+ Clean/Frosted/Textured/Subtle/Standard/Immersive/Dashboard/Form/ModalGlassContainer)
target: Express presets as token-level recipes on OptimizedGlass (intent/elevation) instead of wrapper components
justification: Unexported, visually blank in certification, duplicated by the OptimizedGlass elevation/intensity API, and its one distinctive preset (textured noise) is broken by a typo. Presets belong in tokens/recipes, not nine wrapper components with magic numbers.

name: GlassQueryBuilder
target: Immutable reducer-based QueryBuilder with typed operators per field type, controlled+uncontrolled support, and theme tokens instead of glass-text-white
justification: A query builder is genuinely useful for dashboard/workflow consumers and it already reuses GlassSelect, but in-place mutation of props, crash on empty fields, non-functional uncontrolled mode and hard-coded white text make it unsafe to ship. Keep the concept, rewrite the state model and theming.

name: GlassReactionBar
target: GlassReactions (advanced/GlassReactions.tsx) as the single reactions component with a 'bar' variant
justification: Three root-exported reaction components is noise. This one is the thinnest - a map over ghost buttons without pressed state or accessible labels. Merge into one reactions API (bar/bubbles variants, aria-pressed, accessible names) and drop this export.

name: GlassSearchInterface
target: GlassCommandPalette / GlassCombobox core (single search+listbox engine), with filters as a separate facet panel
justification: The focus trap makes the search box unusable for typing, it lacks combobox semantics, and it silently renders fake catalog data in production. The library already has CommandPalette, SpotlightSearch and Combobox; merge into one accessible search/listbox engine and migrate GlassListView.

name: GlassSignaturePad
target: If needed for forms, rebuild on signature_pad (MIT) with DPR scaling, pointer capture, typed-signature fallback and form value integration; otherwise drop
justification: Not exported, so no consumer depends on it. The placeholder is baked into exported images, controlled mode wipes the canvas, it is blurry on HiDPI and overflows mobile. A signature field is a legitimate form primitive but this one is not salvageable as-is.

name: GlassSpotlight
target: Tour/Coachmark built on primitives/dismissable-layer + positioning, anchor-element based, tokenised scrim material
justification: Spotlight/coachmarks are a premium-feel pattern and this is one of the more visually considered files (highest contrast in its screenshot), but it is bespoke CSS outside the material system, has no dialog semantics or focus handling, uses static DOMRects and runs a 60fps React state loop for a demo orb. Rebuild on the existing overlay primitives.

name: GlassStepper (interactive)
target: src/components/input/GlassStepper.tsx / GlassFormStepper - one Stepper with completed/active/upcoming states
justification: Three steppers exist, two share the exact name, and the root exports the weakest one (no completion state, unused optional flag, runtime-built Tailwind class, misfiring pulse). Consolidate into a single Stepper API and remove this file.

name: GlassTagInput
target: GlassMultiSelect / GlassCombobox (creatable multi mode)
justification: Tag input is a common need, but this version overrides the shared material with inline rgba, has unlabelled controls, mouse-only suggestions and is controlled-only. GlassMultiSelect/Combobox already cover chips+listbox; add a 'creatable' mode there and retire this export.

name: GlassThemeDemo
target: Move to Storybook/docs site as an MDX showcase page
justification: A demo page has no place in the package's public API and inflates bundle/import graph. Its code samples document a different library (MUI), and its metrics panel is placeholder text. Move the showcase into docs, rewrite snippets against the real API, and drop the export.

name: GlassThemeSwitcher
target: ThemeSwitcher bound to the theme subpath provider (useGlassTheme), segmented-control/radiogroup semantics, real system detection
justification: A theme switcher is a core design-system piece, but this one is a mouse-only grid of divs with hard-coded preview colours that does not actually change the theme or detect system preference. Rebuild as a radiogroup/segmented control wired to the real theme provider.

name: GlassUserPresence
target: GlassPresenceIndicator + GlassAvatar(status) composed into a PresenceList recipe
justification: Three presence components exist; this one duplicates its own helpers, uses raw Tailwind status colours and a hard-coded black avatar ring, and has typo'd/no-op classes. Fold the useful parts (list grouping, status setter) into a PresenceList built on GlassAvatar status and GlassPresenceIndicator tokens.

name: [internal] UserPresenceItem / GlassVirtualGrid / preset wrapper containers
target: Follow parent disposition
justification: Noted for completeness; not separately scored. They follow the fate of their parent files.

name: GlassVideoPlayer
target: GlassAdvancedVideoPlayer (media/) - single player, after fixing scoped keyboard shortcuts and slider semantics
justification: Two root-exported video players; this one has dead settings/PiP features, a non-accessible seek bar and a page-wide keyboard hijack that breaks any form on the same page. Merge into the media player, scope shortcuts to the focused player, and use a real slider for seek/volume.

name: GlassVirtualList (+ GlassVirtualGrid)
target: @tanstack/react-virtual behind the existing useVirtualization hook; expose renderItem API and reuse in GlassVirtualTable/MessageList
justification: Virtualisation is infrastructure, not a visual component, and this hand-rolled version is wrong for variable heights, spams onEndReached and has no a11y semantics. Replace the engine with a proven virtualizer behind useVirtualization, and keep a thin glass-styled list wrapper only if needed.

name: GlassVoiceInput
target: VoiceGlassControl (voice/) remains the single voice component
justification: Unexported duplicate of VoiceGlassControl with twelve stories advertising inert controls, an exponentially growing rAF leak, a canvas gradient that throws on real audio, and non-functional wake-word. Delete it; if voice is kept, harden VoiceGlassControl instead.

name: GlassWhiteboard
target: GlassSharedWhiteboard (single Whiteboard with real pointer events, controlled data, adapter-based collaboration)
justification: A working-but-naive canvas sketchpad dressed as a collaborative whiteboard. Three advertised props are dead, the eraser paints white, canvas color handling is broken for var() tokens, there is no touch/pointer support, no DPR scaling, no undo, and the a11y story is role=application with nothing behind it. It overlaps almost entirely with GlassSharedWhiteboard, which is also root-exported. Merge into one Whiteboard built on Pointer Events with controlled document state, a collaboration adapter interface (not a boolean), destination-out erasing, DPR-aware rendering and token-resolved colors; deprecate this export behind an alias for one major.

name: LiquidGlassCommandSurface
target: GlassCommandPalette (rebuilt on the library Dialog/Portal/FocusScope + combobox primitives, with LiquidGlassMaterial as a material option)
justification: Command palettes are a flagship-grade surface in premium systems, but this is the weakest of four overlapping implementations: no dialog semantics, broken combobox ARIA, missing utility classes that silently drop z-index and list height, light-only hard-coded colors that defeat the LiquidGlassMaterial primitive, and styling that only looks right because the story injects CSS. Fold its one useful idea (Liquid material + scroll edge) into a single CommandPalette as material='liquid'.

name: LiquidGlassMapControls
target: Keep as thin recipe over LiquidGlassControlGroup; implement placement CSS, toolbar role + roving focus, intrinsic 44px targets, pressed state, remove inline gradient
justification: Small and honest in scope, built on the right primitive, and map/floating-control clusters are a legitimate Liquid Glass pattern. But the placement prop does nothing, the inline gradient overrides the material variant, keyboard roving focus is advertised but absent, and touch targets/typography live in the story instead of the component. Fix those and it is a reasonable recipe; it does not justify a standalone flagship.

name: PageTransitionDemo
target: Move as a story example for GlassPageTransition (src/components/animations/GlassTransitions.tsx:258)
justification: Not exported from the root, fixed-size, placeholder content, broken gradients, invisible white labels on a light background, and reduced-motion is imported but ignored. It is demo code living in src/components and inflating the component count. Delete it and, if the pattern is wanted, show it as a GlassPageTransition story.

name: ThemedGlassComponents
target: OptimizedGlass (elevation prop) / theme provider
justification: Not publicly exported, functionally a renamed OptimizedGlass, with dead props, an unstyled 'transition' class driven by setTimeout, and Tailwind classes that only exist in the Storybook shim. Its story is blank. Remove it and its tests; nothing in the public API depends on it.

name: Box
target: Single layout primitive set: Box (polymorphic, asChild via primitives/slot) merged with GlassBox system-props variant
justification: Box is a 30-line div wrapper whose only behavior is adding transition-all to every node, which is a perf and visual-jank liability, and it shares its name with a second incompatible Box in GlassBox.tsx. Keep one polymorphic primitive (as/asChild, no default transitions, no 'use client'), and fold GlassBox's glass variant into it as a prop or a separate Surface component.

name: ContentSection
target: AppShell redesign (Section slot) or GlassCard
justification: Useful pattern but undocumented, unstoried, untested, and its default shimmer is wrong for content. Fold into the redesigned shell/page primitives.

name: GlassAppShell
target: Single AppShell (absorb ZSpaceAppLayout) with explicit slots/context instead of cloneElement-by-displayName
justification: An app shell is a flagship surface for a premium system, but this one hard-codes light-theme text and shadow values on the root, ships a Tailwind gradient class the library CSS does not contain, defaults to role='application', and couples to GlassSidebar/GlassHeader by displayName string. Redesign around a shell context (sidebar state controlled/uncontrolled, mobile drawer with focus trap), token-driven material layers, CSS-container-query responsiveness, and merge ZSpaceAppLayout's depth idea as an optional material treatment.

name: GlassBox
target: GlassSurface / OptimizedGlass primitive (glass) + single Box primitive (layout)
justification: GlassBox is a thin preset over OptimizedGlass bolted onto a second MUI-style system-props Box whose spacing props compile to Tailwind classes that the library does not ship. It duplicates layout/Box under the same exported name and duplicates every other 'glass panel' in the library. Replace with one material primitive (Surface) plus token-based spacing props that emit inline CSS variables, not class names.

name: GlassContainer
target: Container (max-width + padding, no glass, server-safe) + Surface material primitive; delete consciousness API
justification: The core job (max-width, centering, padding) is trivial, yet this file bundles five 'advanced' engines, violates the rules of hooks, likely nulls forwarded refs, and markets mock biometric/eye-tracking behavior. It is also used internally by GlassAppShell and ZSpaceAppLayout, so its weight and bugs propagate. Rebuild as a server-safe Container plus an opt-in Surface material, and remove ConsciousGlassContainer/withConsciousness/ConsciousnessPresets.

name: GlassFlex
target: Stack (single flex primitive with responsive object props implemented via CSS variables + container queries)
justification: Flex, Stack, HStack, VStack (x2) and Box all solve the same problem with slightly different prop names (direction 'col' vs 'vertical', gap vs space vs spacing). The responsive API advertised here does not function. Collapse into one Stack/Flex primitive with working responsive props and no 'Glass' prefix.

name: GlassGrid
target: Grid primitive emitting grid-template-columns via CSS variables (repeat(var(--cols),minmax(0,1fr))) with responsive/auto-fit support
justification: The story uses cols={4}, one of only three column classes that exist in the shipped CSS, which is why certification passed. In real consumption most column counts and all responsive overrides silently fail. A grid primitive must be self-contained; rebuild with inline CSS variables and export GridItem.

name: GlassMasonry
target: components/layouts/GlassMasonryGrid (or a single Masonry with responsive columns)
justification: Two masonry components are exported from root. This one is a 40-line column-count wrapper with wrong ARIA roles and no responsive behavior. Merge into one Masonry with responsive column count, no grid roles, and tokenized gaps.

name: GlassScrollArea
target: ScrollArea on native overflow with LiquidGlassScrollEdge edge treatment; drop fake custom scrollbar or implement properly (Radix-like)
justification: Visually it can pass a screenshot because the native thin scrollbar and edge fades look acceptable, but most of its 620 lines (custom bars, thumb drag, useScrollArea) do not work. Rebuild as a lean native-scroll region with focusable scroller, scroll-edge material from the primitives layer, and no default shimmer.

name: GlassSeparator
target: data-display/GlassDivider -> single Separator primitive (token hairline, specular gradient via CSS vars)
justification: Separator and Divider are both exported; this one has variants that depend on classes the library doesn't ship, an un-generatable length class, and a wrapper div that breaks vertical layout. One Separator with a token-driven hairline (and an optional refracted/specular edge) is all that's needed.

name: GlassSplitPane
target: ResizablePanels (pointer events, container-relative math, controlled value, orientation-aware keys, 24px hit area)
justification: The keyboard ARIA is a decent start, but the core drag behavior is wrong outside full-viewport usage and absent on touch. Rebuild with pointer capture and container-relative sizing, controlled/uncontrolled values, and a single material layer.

name: GlassStack
target: Becomes the single Stack primitive (absorbs GlassFlex, HStack, VStack); fix responsive props; rename to Stack
justification: Of the overlapping flex primitives, GlassStack has the best API (token gaps, dividers) and is already used internally (GlassAppShell imports VStack from it). Keep it as the survivor, but fix the responsive implementation (CSS variables per breakpoint), drop transition-all, drop 'use client', and delete the duplicate HStack/VStack files.

name: HStack
target: GlassStack (Stack direction='horizontal' / its HStack alias)
justification: A second HStack implementation that adds a wrapper div and fake glass props. Re-point the root export to the GlassStack alias and delete this file.

name: OptimizedGlassContainer
target: A single app-level GlassQualityProvider (one shared FPS/device-tier probe) consumed by OptimizedGlass/Surface
justification: Performance adaptation belongs at the provider level, measured once; a per-container rAF loop that re-renders its subtree every second is itself a performance problem. Deprecate in favor of a shared quality tier read by the material primitive.

name: VStack
target: GlassStack (VStack alias)
justification: Copy-paste duplicate of HStack.tsx; delete and export the GlassStack alias from root.

name: ZSpaceAppLayout
target: GlassAppShell (redesigned) with an optional 'depth' material treatment
justification: A second app shell with no mobile navigation path, missing landmarks, five nested blur layers and a depth gimmick with no visible payoff. Merge any valuable layering/elevation ideas into the single redesigned AppShell.

name: GlassFractalLayout
justification: A novelty demo with no real product use case: the 'fractal' types are mislabeled positioning presets (mandelbrot/julia are fake), nodes are not keyboard reachable, springs are misconfigured for framer-motion, and the visible chrome is a debug HUD ('Type/Depth/Nodes/Zoom' badges L512-529). 24 stories on a component nobody should ship inflate surface area. Remove from 5.0; if a tree visualization is wanted it belongs in a data-viz package built on a real layout algorithm.

name: GlassGoldenRatioGrid
justification: A gimmick layout with a debug HUD ('Sections/Items/Golden Ratio/Levels' L561-576), fake ARIA grid semantics, render-phase side effects, and unused sizing props. Real apps use CSS grid; a premium design system does not ship a 'golden ratio' grid with a dashed gold spiral overlay. Remove.

name: GlassIslandLayout
justification: A half-built node-graph editor: resizing is a stub, connection colors silently fail on canvas, physics re-subscribes rAF every frame, controls are unlabeled emoji, and the minimize control is keyboard-unreachable. Not salvageable as a design-system primitive; a real canvas/graph editor is application territory (React Flow etc.). Deprecate in 5.0, remove in 6.0.

name: GlassMasonryGrid
target: src/components/layout/GlassMasonry.tsx
justification: Masonry is a legitimate need, but this implementation is a demo panel (hard-coded header, stats HUD, footer 'Grid: WxH px') wrapped around broken features: search loses focus each keystroke, drag-reorder is a no-op, virtualization ignores scroll, sentinel leaks. The 107-line GlassMasonry already exists. Consolidate into one headless masonry (CSS columns or measured layout) with optional toolbar composition; drop the stats/filters baked into the layout.

name: GlassOrbitalMenu
target: GlassFab speed-dial / radial variant
justification: A radial menu is a plausible signature interaction for a Liquid Glass system, and the open/close semantics are partially right, but it needs a rebuild: per-item Liquid material instead of a glass box, roving tabindex + arrow keys + Escape, labels on focus, real framer spring params (stiffness/damping), and no 60fps setState rotation. Fold into a GlassFab 'radial' variant rather than a standalone 'layout'.

name: GlassTessellation
justification: No glass material on the tiles, no keyboard access, misconfigured motion, and the geometry doesn't actually tessellate. Pure novelty. Remove; salvage getReadableTextColor (L113-125) into the shared contrast utilities if not already duplicated there.

name: AuroraBackground
justification: The cleanest backdrop in the shard: tokenized, deterministic, SSR-safe, and the only component here with genuinely correct reduced-motion and forced-colors handling. It should become THE canonical atmospheric backdrop and absorb GlassAuroraDisplay/AuroraPro (DEPRECATE those). Polish: drop 'use client', reconcile 'ag-' vs 'glass-' naming, add more stories (palettes x intensity x light/dark), and get it into the visual certification set (no screenshot slug exists).

name: AuroraOrb
justification: Small, correct, cheap. It's a gradient sphere, not glass, so it's decoration for marketing pages only. Fix aria-hidden-with-children, keep in the ./marketing subpath, and avoid promoting it as a material showcase.

name: DisplayText
justification: Correct and tiny, but typographically generic: default Georgia fallback and zero tracking make hero text look like a blog, not a first-party system. Ship a real display type scale (font, optical tracking per size) in tokens, drop 'use client', and align with the main typography components so there aren't two heading systems.

name: FeatureTile
justification: Good compositional pattern, but tone variants are fake (no CSS for data-tone) and the heading level is fixed. Add headingLevel/as, implement or remove tones, verify index-badge contrast.

name: InstallCommand
justification: Accessible and small, but it's AuraGlass-docs chrome shipped as a library component. Generalize into a CopyableCode/Snippet (package name not baked in), reset copied state after timeout, catch clipboard errors, and compose ShowcaseCard instead of borrowing its class string.

name: LogoMark
justification: It is the AuraGlass brand glyph rendered generically (rounded square of gradient). Fine for the docs/marketing subpath; does not belong in the root barrel. Move to ./marketing only and keep as brand asset.

name: ShowcaseCard
target: src/components/card/GlassCard.tsx
justification: Good, token-driven CSS card — but it is a second card material system alongside GlassCard/OptimizedGlass/LiquidGlassMaterial. Fold its data-attribute + CSS-variable approach into GlassCard as the canonical implementation (or make ShowcaseCard a GlassCard preset) so there is one card material in 5.0.

name: GlassAdvancedAudioPlayer
target: LiquidGlassMediaControls + headless useMediaElement hook
justification: Feature list is fiction: mock waveform, mock transcripts, playlist that doesn't change tracks, play/pause that can't pause without hidden provider registration, a RegExp crash on search, emoji icons, canvas colors that silently fail. Rebuild as a composition: headless media hook bound to the <audio> element as source of truth, LiquidGlassMediaControls for transport, icon set instead of emoji, real slider semantics, optional transcript slot fed by consumer data.

name: GlassAdvancedVideoPlayer
target: single GlassVideoPlayer (merge with src/components/interactive/GlassVideoPlayer.tsx) built on LiquidGlassMediaControls
justification: Two video players exist; this one has fake quality switching, no keyboard model, hover-only volume, no captions, emoji iconography, hard-coded blue selection, and a Storybook-only poster swap that means the certification never saw a video. A media player is a strong flagship opportunity for Liquid Glass (floating controls over content is exactly the material's use case), but it must be rebuilt: element-as-source-of-truth state, slider semantics, keyboard shortcuts, <track> captions, LiquidGlassMaterial controls with local dimming.

name: GlassMediaProvider
target: headless useMediaElement(ref) hook + optional lightweight MediaSession context; no built-in AI
justification: Ships fake AI (canned transcripts with invented speaker names and random confidence/sentiment) in a production library — a credibility liability. Architecturally it duplicates the media element's state, requires undocumented registration for play() to work, re-renders all consumers on every time update, and leaks recording streams. Replace with a headless hook where the HTMLMediaElement is the single source of truth; transcripts/chapters become consumer-supplied data; recording moves out of the design system.

name: LiquidGlassMediaControls
justification: The only honest media component in the shard: controlled, native semantics, built on LiquidGlassMaterial. It should become the canonical transport bar that both advanced players compose. Needs: real icon glyphs, tokenized range track/thumb styling (no #64748b), aria-valuetext with formatted time, skip/next slots, adaptive tint, and real visual certification (no screenshot slug exists). With that work, 'floating Liquid Glass controls over video' is a credible flagship screenshot.

name: LiquidGlassNowPlayingBar
justification: Correct composition on the Liquid primitives and a familiar OS-native pattern. Polish: icons instead of words, progressbar semantics, aria-expanded for the expand affordance, next/prev slots, and replace the audio player's 'compact' variant with this.

name: LiquidGlassPhotoInspector
target: src/components/navigation/LiquidGlassInspectorPanel.tsx (as a documented recipe/preset)
justification: 48 lines of section config over the inspector panel; doesn't warrant its own public component. Make it a story/recipe of LiquidGlassInspectorPanel, and fix the panel's static section ids and 'x' close glyph, plus skip empty sections.

name: GlassActionSheet
target: Single GlassSheet (side=bottom) built on primitives/portal + FocusScope + DismissableLayer, with an 'actions' preset
justification: An iOS-style action sheet is a legitimate pattern, but this is one of at least five independent bottom-sheet implementations in the library. It has a rules-of-hooks bug on the liquid path, no focus management, colliding static ids, and its animation depends on Tailwind classes the package does not ship. The behavior should become a preset of one canonical sheet that owns portal, focus, dismissal and motion.

name: GlassPullToRefresh
justification: Functionally honest and reasonably small. It needs an announced status region, aria-busy, reduced-motion handling, a ref-based pull distance so listeners stop re-binding every frame, and surfaced error state. Only one story exists and it cannot show the pulled state, so the visual is unproven.

name: AdaptiveGlassDensity
justification: It does nothing it claims, and it hides content from reduced-motion users. Remove it.

name: MobileGlassBottomSheet
target: GlassSheet (canonical)
justification: This is the fifth bottom sheet. It is invisible for reduced-motion users, has no dialog semantics, and its snap points are broken.

name: MobileGlassNavigation
target: useSwipe hook
justification: A misnamed swipe wrapper with no navigation semantics and no keyboard path. It should be a hook if the behavior is kept at all.

name: TouchOptimizedGlass (alias TouchGlassOptimization)
target: usePress/useRipple hooks + GlassPressable primitive
justification: A touch-only surface that blocks scrolling and clicks, has no keyboard path, and whose intensity API does nothing. Ripple and press feedback belong in a shared interaction hook that every pressable glass control uses, not in a wrapper component.

name: TouchRippleEffects
target: useRipple hook shared with GlassButton
justification: This is the same ripple implemented a second time in the same file. Fold it into one pointer-event ripple hook.

name: GlassBottomSheet
target: GlassSheet (canonical, side=bottom) on Portal/FocusScope/DismissableLayer
justification: The closed state appears to leave the sheet visible, hooks are called conditionally, there is no focus trap, and the z-index class does not exist. A bottom sheet is a glass-signature surface, so the concept should survive as one canonical sheet with real detents, drag, and focus management.

name: GlassDialog
target: GlassModal -> canonical GlassDialog rebuilt on Portal/FocusScope/DismissableLayer
justification: This is a 1,059-line near-copy of GlassModal. Roughly half of it is fake consciousness telemetry that causes per-second re-renders. Its focus trap is real, but role=dialog sits on the backdrop wrapper, props and className are duplicated, it is not portaled, and the dialog surface lifts on hover. Merge it into one dialog.

name: GlassDrawer
target: GlassSheet (side=left|right|top|bottom) on shared primitives
justification: This is a modal drawer with no focus management, conditional hooks, colliding ids, an open=true default, and width classes the package does not ship. It also imports the advanced 'consciousness' modules for features that are stubs. Fold it into a single sheet primitive with side variants.

name: GlassHoverCard
target: GlassPopover rebuilt on primitives/positioning (hover-intent mode)
justification: This is a third hand-rolled floating-position engine (alongside Popover and Tooltip) in a library that already ships Positioner, Portal and DismissableLayer primitives used by GlassDropdownMenu. It is mouse-only with the wrong role. Make it a hover-intent mode of one floating primitive.

name: GlassModal
