target: Canonical GlassDialog/GlassSheet family (absorbs GlassDialog, GlassDrawer, GlassBottomSheet, GlassActionSheet, LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet, MobileGlassBottomSheet)
justification: This is the most correct overlay in the shard (real FocusTrap, focus restore, scroll lock, alertdialog support) and the richest material stack, so it is the right base for a flagship dialog. It still needs to drop the consciousness mocks, call hooks unconditionally, portal through primitives/portal, use onOpenChange with a false default, add exit animation via AnimatePresence, and make the blur scale real. It then becomes the single overlay engine for sheet and drawer variants.

name: GlassPopover
target: GlassPopover on primitives/positioning + portal + dismissable-layer (canonical floating surface for Popover/HoverCard/Tooltip/Menu)
justification: Its controlled/uncontrolled API and FocusTrap are a good base. It reimplements positioning and flip logic by hand instead of using the library's own Positioner, and it nests a near-opaque bg-background/95 inside glass. The role is on the wrong element, and it ships a conflicting second GlassTooltip. Rebuild it as the single floating primitive.

name: GlassTooltip
target: GlassTooltip on primitives/positioning + portal (focus+hover, Escape, describedby on trigger)
justification: A tooltip is a foundational primitive, and this one is mouse-only, mispositioned on first paint, and paired with no-op compound parts. Its stories fake the visual with a static div. Two components share the GlassTooltip name with different APIs. Rebuild it on the shared floating primitive and delete the duplicate.

name: LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet
target: GlassSheet material='liquid' using LiquidGlassSourceTransition for real source morphs
justification: It uses the right primitive, but the Liquid Glass promise (adaptive detents, source morph, dark/light adaptation) is not implemented: it is a static light-only panel with hard-coded slate text and no motion. It should become the liquid material variant of the canonical sheet, which already has the focus and motion engine.

name: LiquidGlassPopoverMenu
target: GlassDropdownMenu (material='liquid')
justification: The library already has a menu primitive with roving focus and positioning. This is an unanchored list of buttons with invalid ARIA and per-instance !important CSS injection. Its liquid look should be a material option on the real menu.

name: CollapsedMenu
target: GlassDropdownMenu (GlassTabBar overflow should render DropdownMenu.Content)
justification: A private overflow popover for GlassTabBar that re-implements menu semantics incorrectly (menuitems inside a navigation landmark, no roving focus, no Escape). The library already has a far more complete GlassDropdownMenu; GlassTabBar should use it and this file should be deleted along with its story/test which only exist to bump coverage.

name: ScrollButtons
target: IconButton with library chevron icons inside GlassTabBar
justification: Trivial internal helper using typographic chevrons and a className bug that emits 'undefined'. Not a design-system component; fold into GlassTabBar using the shared IconButton and @/icons ChevronLeft/Right.

name: TabItem
target: GlassTabItem / single Tabs primitive
justification: Keyboard handling is actually decent, but it is a second private tab-trigger implementation with hard-coded rgba and px values while a public GlassTabItem exists. Merge into one tab trigger used by every tab component.

name: EnhancedGlassTabs
target: GlassPageTabs (or a single unified GlassTabs)
justification: One of at least six tab implementations, and the one whose marketing ('accessibility-focused') is most contradicted by code: keyboard users cannot change tabs, panels it claims to control do not exist, the color prop is dead, and its motion classes cannot compile. GlassPageTabs already does APG-correct tabs; deprecate this with a codemod mapping tabs/activeTab/onChange to tabs/value/onChange.

name: GlassBottomNav
target: Merge with LiquidGlassTabBar as a single link-based bottom tab bar
justification: The core mobile chrome surface, but it misuses tab semantics for navigation, traps keyboard users on the active item, ignores href and elevation, and stacks a GlassButton pill inside a glass slab rather than reading as an iOS-grade tab bar. Rebuild on LiquidGlassMaterial with nav/a + aria-current, asChild for router links and real safe-area insets.

name: GlassBreadcrumb (+ GlassBreadcrumbItem, GlassBreadcrumbSeparator, GlassBreadcrumbLink, GlassBreadcrumbCompound)
target: single Breadcrumb family (merge with app-shell GlassBreadcrumbs; export Item/Link/Separator)
justification: Structurally sound breadcrumb with correct list semantics, but three breadcrumb implementations exist, the compound parts are not publicly exported, the style-spread bug defeats the contained/maxWidth features, and maxItems math is duplicated and wrong at edge values. Merge into one family with asChild links.

name: GlassCommandBar
target: LiquidGlassToolbar / GlassToolbar
justification: A 111-line button row that overlaps five other toolbar/action-bar components and lacks the toolbar keyboard model its role promises. Fold into the toolbar family as a 'compact actions' variant.

name: GlassContextMenu (+ GlassContextMenuContent, GlassContextMenuItem, useContextMenu)
target: GlassContextMenu rebuilt on GlassDropdownMenu content/item primitives (Positioner at pointer, DismissableLayer, FocusScope autoFocus)
justification: The outside-click handler closes the menu on mousedown inside it, so the primary interaction (click an item) is broken; there is no keyboard entry, default positioning ignores the cursor, and material is double-stacked. The dropdown family already has DismissableLayer/Positioner/FocusScope - rebuild the context menu as a thin trigger over those.

name: GlassDropdownMenu (+ Trigger, Content, Item, CheckboxItem, RadioGroup, RadioItem, Label, Separator, Shortcut, Sub, SubTrigger, SubContent)
justification: The only menu in the library with a credible primitive architecture (controllable state, Slot, Positioner, DismissableLayer, FocusScope, sub-menus). It should become the single menu engine for context menu, menubar, header user menu and tab overflow. Required polish: Enter/Space activation, autofocus first item on open, typeahead, visible radio indicator, replace hard-coded rgba/blur with the shared Liquid Glass material and tokens, remove dead tailwindcss-animate classes.

name: GlassHeader (+ internal NotificationButton, UserMenu; exported-from-file HeaderBreadcrumbs, HeaderNavigation, ConsciousGlassHeader, PredictiveHeader, GazeResponsiveHeader, AccessibleHeader, HeaderConsciousnessPresets)
target: GlassTopBar (app-shell) composed with GlassDropdownMenu, GlassBreadcrumb and a real search combobox
justification: The library's primary header ships fake product data, conditional hooks, a 240-line duplicated render path, double navigation landmarks, global DOM querying, full-page click catchers and ~6.4k lines of pseudo-scientific 'consciousness' imports. None of that belongs in a premium first-party header. Replace with a slim, slot-based top bar (app-shell GlassTopBar) and delete the Conscious/Predictive/Gaze/Accessible variants and presets.

name: GlassMenubar (+ GlassMenubarContent, GlassMenubarItem, useMenubar, createFileMenu, createEditMenu)
target: Menubar built on GlassDropdownMenu primitives (Menubar.Menu/Trigger/Content)
justification: Recursive self-nesting produces invalid menubar-in-menu semantics, hover closes submenus before the pointer can reach them, separators double-render, and the visual is a stack of bordered pills. A desktop-app menubar is valuable for a premium kit but must be rebuilt as a compound API over the dropdown engine.

name: GlassMenuPrimitive (Root, Content, Item)
target: GlassDropdownMenu internals (+ src/primitives roving-focus)
justification: A second, weaker menu primitive alongside the dropdown engine, with hard-coded item chrome that makes the menubar look like a button stack. Collapse into one headless menu primitive (shared by dropdown, context, menubar) with material applied from tokens.

name: GlassMobileNav
justification: Solid dialog mechanics (focus trap, inert, scroll lock, reduced motion) make this the most production-ready nav surface here, but items must render real links with aria-current, the fake push/slide variants and ignored elevation should be removed or implemented, and the white scrim should be theme-aware. Longer term it should be the Sheet primitive + a nav list rather than a standalone drawer.

name: GlassNavigation (alias GlassNavbar)
target: GlassTopBar (app-shell) + GlassSidebar for vertical
justification: A catch-all navbar whose icons are a placeholder emoji, whose tooltips are title attributes, whose spring/intensity props are dead, and whose responsive toggle depends on Tailwind classes the package does not ship. It overlaps the header, sidebar and app-shell top bar. Remove (keep GlassNavbar alias pointing at the replacement for one major).

name: GlassNavigationMenu (+ GlassNavigationMenuContent, GlassNavigationMenuItem, useNavigationMenu, createDashboardNavigation, createAdminNavigation)
target: GlassSidebar / LiquidGlassInsetSidebar nav tree
justification: A disclosure nav list that hard-navigates with window.location, renders links as buttons, nests landmarks and glass-in-glass, and ships emoji demo presets. Its job is the sidebar tree; merge into the sidebar family with link/asChild items.

name: GlassPageTabs
justification: The reference implementation in this shard: real APG keyboard model, tokenised CSS-module material with specular layer, reduced-motion/transparency/forced-colors handling, SSR-safe ids. It should be the base of a single Tabs family (add compound parts, dark-theme ink tokens, size scale, tests, and a certification screenshot) and the other five tab components should be deprecated into it.

name: GlassPagination (+ GlassPaginationContent, GlassPaginationItem, usePagination, GlassPaginationWithInfo)
justification: Page-range logic is fine and the item-info compound is useful, but the controls are non-focusable divs (keyboard users cannot paginate at all) and each button stacks its own backdrop-filter, which is both visually noisy and expensive. Rebuild with real <button>/<a> items (asChild for router links), a single glass container, aria-current on the active page, and share it with the data-table paginators.

name: GlassResponsiveNav (alias ResponsiveNavigation)
target: GlassAppShell (app-shell) with CSS container/media-query driven chrome
justification: A JS-breakpoint switcher that inherits all of BottomNav's and MobileNav's defects, flashes desktop chrome on mobile first paint, fakes the 'sidebar' tablet mode and emits href='#' links. Responsive chrome belongs in the app-shell layout via CSS, not a runtime innerWidth listener.

name: GlassSegmentedControl
target: single SegmentedControl (merge with LiquidGlassSegmentedControl and GlassToggleGroup)
justification: A segmented control is a signature Liquid Glass component (iOS/macOS), so it should be a flagship, but this implementation is a row of independent GlassButtons inside a glass track with no shared sliding thumb, wrong landmark semantics (nav + group with duplicate labels), no arrow-key/radio semantics, and icon-only mode loses accessible names. Two parallel implementations (glass vs liquid) with different prop names (items/onChange vs segments/onValueChange). Redesign as one component with a measured, spring-animated thumb on the liquid material, radiogroup semantics, controlled/uncontrolled, and consolidate the duplicates into it.

name: GlassSidebar
target: single Sidebar in app-shell (merge LiquidGlassInsetSidebar, GlassSidebarRail/Panel)
justification: The sidebar is a core app-shell flagship surface, but this one has two real correctness bugs (uncontrolled collapse never toggles; hooks after a conditional return crash when overlay open flips), a broken active-state class, ignored hrefs (no real links / aria-current), runtime-interpolated Tailwind classes that never compile, and a body-portaled toggle that is positioned by measuring the viewport. It duplicates three other sidebars. Redesign one sidebar on the liquid material with proper link semantics, disclosure semantics for groups, controlled/uncontrolled state and an in-flow toggle.

name: SidebarBrand / SidebarUserInfo
target: Sidebar slots in redesigned app-shell Sidebar; use GlassAvatar
justification: Not exported from root (only module-level exports), unstoried, untested, and re-implements avatar/status that GlassAvatar already has. Fold into slot API of the redesigned sidebar.

name: GlassTabBar
target: GlassTabs (redesigned headless-tablist with animated liquid indicator)
justification: 1,200 lines of fake complexity: the 'physics' selector cannot work because tab refs are never attached, index-0 is treated as unselected, the component's own keyboard handler and magnetic-trail component are never wired, and a dozen props are no-ops. Its value (pill indicator CSS in the module) can be salvaged into a single Tabs implementation. Replace with the consolidated GlassTabs and keep GlassTabBar as a deprecated alias for one major.

name: GlassTabItem
target: GlassTabsTrigger
justification: A third standalone tab-item implementation with off-token inline styles, a per-instance injected stylesheet with a garish !important accent hover, link-as-tab semantics, and an indicator that disappears under reduced motion. Nothing composes it. Deprecate in favour of the trigger of the consolidated Tabs.

name: GlassTabs (GlassTabs, GlassTabsList, GlassTabsTrigger, GlassTabsContent)
target: canonical Tabs; absorb GlassTabBar, GlassTabItem, EnhancedGlassTabs, GlassPageTabs, LiquidGlassTabBar (as variant='liquid'/placement='bottom')
justification: The only tab implementation in this shard with a sound compound API and near-correct WAI-ARIA tabs semantics, so it should become the canonical Tabs. To meet the premium bar it needs a real shared animated indicator on the liquid material (the measured ink is currently dead code), roving tabindex, useId-based ids, removal of the scaleIn-per-trigger mount animation, removal of the className.includes layout hack, and the controlled-'' bug fix.

name: GlassToolbar
target: single Toolbar (merge LiquidGlassToolbar; liquid as default material)
justification: Functional slot layout on the shared primitive, but wrong landmark role, no roving focus, and two parallel implementations with diverging semantics. Merge with LiquidGlassToolbar into one role=toolbar component with roving-focus groups.

name: HeaderUserMenu
target: GlassDropdownMenu / GlassMenuPrimitive recipe (AccountMenu pattern)
justification: Not exported from the package root or any subpath, so it is effectively dead public surface despite stories/tests. It re-implements a dropdown menu without menu semantics or keyboard support, with no-op props and invented utility classes. Rebuild as a thin recipe on GlassMenuPrimitive (role=menu, roving focus) or drop.

name: LiquidGlassBottomAccessory
target: BottomTabBar.Accessory sub-component
justification: A 29-line pill wrapper; correct material usage, but as a standalone export it adds API surface without behaviour (collapsed is fake). Make it a slot/sub-component of the redesigned bottom tab bar with a real collapse transition.

name: LiquidGlassInsetSidebar
target: redesigned app-shell Sidebar (variant='inset')
justification: The 'inset' presentation is the right modern look, but the component is a flat list of buttons with three no-op Apple-named props and a hard-coded white fill. Make it the inset variant of the single redesigned Sidebar.

name: LiquidGlassInspectorPanel
target: GlassInspectorPanel (src/workspace/index.tsx)
justification: Correct material and scroll-edge primitives, but a literal 'x' close glyph, native CSS resize, no enter/exit transition, no Escape, and placement that does nothing. There is already a GlassInspectorPanel in workspace; merge into that one and give it a real resize handle, icon close button and slide transition.

name: LiquidGlassSegmentedControl
target: GlassSegmentedControl (redesigned, liquid material default)
justification: Thin wrapper that uses the right primitives then neutralises them with hard-coded white rgba fills; selected state is barely distinguishable because inline color overrides the selected class; density is fake; 1-line test. Fold its primitive usage into the redesigned single SegmentedControl and delete.

name: LiquidGlassTabBar
target: BottomTabBar (merge GlassBottomNav) built on consolidated Tabs semantics
justification: A floating Liquid Glass bottom tab bar with minimize-on-scroll and a bottom accessory is exactly the iOS 26 flagship pattern, but this is a props-only imitation: broken tab semantics (no tablist), icon-only minimized tabs without names, abrupt minimize with no morph, and duplicate behaviours. Redesign as the flagship mobile tab bar with a spring-animated selection lens, proper tablist/keyboard, and animated minimize respecting reduced motion; merge GlassBottomNav.

name: LiquidGlassToolbar
target: single Toolbar
justification: Uses the liquid primitives but neuters the material with a fixed white gradient, ships unstyled buttons without interaction states, and advertises scrollEdge/floating that do nothing. Fold its groups API into the consolidated Toolbar.

name: TabBarContainer / TabSelector (styled.tsx)
target: absorbed into consolidated Tabs indicator styles
justification: Internal leftovers from a styled-components migration; only GlassTabBar uses them. The selector gradient CSS is the one reusable asset; move it into the consolidated tabs stylesheet and animate with transform instead of left/width.

name: GlassCoherenceIndicator
target: Move to @aura-glass/labs (or remove); use GlassGauge/GlassProgress for real metrics
justification: This is a themed random-number widget with no product use case in a premium design system. It has invalid CSS color math, a style object passed as a className, render-time randomness, a non-reactive main prop, and no meter semantics. Eighteen stories inflate coverage for a novelty.

name: GlassProbabilityCloud
justification: It is broken by construction: a 60fps React re-render loop re-randomizes particles every tick, the advertised realTimeMode can never fire, it is not responsive, and it is inaccessible. It has no place in a production design system.

name: GlassQuantumField
justification: Its controls ignore input, its render loop costs O(n*m) per frame and re-subscribes every frame, and it is a fixed-size canvas with no semantics. The story is tuned to hide all of this. Remove it from the core package.

name: GlassQuantumTunnel
justification: This is a decorative pseudo-physics demo with a bespoke duplicated material, undefined utility classes, per-instance style injection, and a likely infinite render loop at default props. It has no product role.

name: GlassSuperpositionalMenu
justification: It is an inaccessible menu that remounts its items 60 times per second and whose selection model is deliberately random. It contradicts what a design system menu is for.

name: GlassWaveFunction
target: Move to labs; a real need is covered by the chart family
justification: This is the least broken quantum component (honest plotting, motion-aware rAF), but it is still a fixed-size canvas demo with CSS variables that canvas ignores, and it does not belong in core. Deprecate it into a labs/demo package.

name: QuantumEntanglementVisualizer
justification: A static demo-data card with the wrong table role, unshipped Tailwind color classes, an inconsistent API, and no tests. A generic stat/metric card already covers any real need.

name: GlassRating
justification: This is a solid, honest control with the best accessibility scaffolding in the shard, but it is an orphan: it is not exported from src/index.ts or any subpath, so consumers cannot import it. Before export it needs: token-based star colors (the Tailwind color classes do not ship, so stars render grey), single aria-checked, focus that follows arrow keys, half-step keyboard support, and uncontrolled defaultValue support.

name: GlassIntelligentSearch
target: Single GlassSearch / GlassCombobox family (with a separate faceted-results recipe)
justification: This is a 1.4k-line monolith that mixes a toy keyword 'NLP' engine, filters, voice and result rendering into one uncontrolled FC, with no ref, no controlled query and an inline stylesheet full of hard-coded white rgba plus !important that bypasses the material system it wraps. The suggestion list has no real combobox keyboard model. The filter and highlight logic is worth keeping as a headless hook. The visual layer should become a recipe on a proper GlassCombobox shared with the five other search components.

name: GlassSpotlightSearch
target: interactive/GlassCommandPalette (single command-palette primitive)
justification: This is a second command palette that is not exported from root, alongside the exported GlassCommandPalette and GlassSpotlight. It has a real stale-closure bug in its keyboard handler, no focus trap, no ARIA listbox semantics, Tailwind classes that do not ship, and an elevation prop that gets clobbered. Merge its recent-actions and grouping features into the canonical command palette and delete this file.

name: LiquidGlassSearchField
target: Become the canonical GlassSearchField/Combobox on LiquidGlassMaterial
justification: This is the right foundation, a small forwardRef on the shared LiquidGlassMaterial, which makes it the best candidate to become the single search field of the 5.0 Liquid Glass line. Today it is incomplete. It has a non-functional placement prop, no keyboard combobox model, label/button nesting, and an !important blur override that fights its own material. It also has only one story, one smoke test and no certification screenshot. Redesign it into a full ARIA combobox (with a headless filter hook shared with GlassIntelligentSearch) and absorb the duplicates.

name: LiquidGlassSearchTab
target: LiquidGlassSearchField (or a LiquidGlassTabBar 'search' slot)
justification: Twenty-five lines that rename props on LiquidGlassSearchField and add only a null-render flag. It inflates the component count without adding capability. If search-in-tab-bar is a real pattern, implement it as a slot on LiquidGlassTabBar.

name: LiquidGlassShowcase
target: Move to Storybook/docs-only example (not a package export)
justification: A propless demo page should not ship in the public API, and this one undermines the system by !important-overriding the Liquid Glass material it is meant to show off. That means the showcase misrepresents what consumers get. Keep it as a docs/story composition after the underlying components look right without overrides.

name: GlassCollaborativeCursor (social)
target: collaboration/GlassCollaborativeCursor
justification: This is the shadowed duplicate. src/index.ts:699 exports the collaboration/ version under the same name, so this file is unreachable for consumers but still certified and storied (18 stories). It is a random-walk demo with baked-in placeholder copy, sounds that play on by default, inline component definitions that remount every tick, and a reduced-motion bug that hides labels. Delete it.

name: GlassPresenceIndicator
target: GlassAvatarGroup + GlassPresenceBadge (single presence primitive)
justification: Presence (avatar plus status dot plus overflow count) is a legitimate pattern, but this version has a reduced-motion invisibility bug, mouse-only interactive chips, colour-only status, sound that fires on every render by default, and a frozen users prop. Fold it into one avatar-group/presence-badge primitive shared with GlassUserPresence and GlassLiveCursorPresence.

name: GlassReactionBubbles
target: interactive/GlassReactionBar (keep one reaction primitive); optional effect as a recipe
justification: This is a novelty effect with a demo-on-by-default state, a setState-per-frame physics loop, invalid className usage that silently drops the glass material, test-env branches inside product code, and a reduced-motion invisibility bug. It is the third reaction component. Keep GlassReactionBar as the product primitive and drop this one, or rewrite it later as an opt-in canvas/WAAPI effect.

name: GlassSharedWhiteboard
target: interactive/GlassWhiteboard (single whiteboard, pointer events + DPR + controlled strokes)
justification: As shipped, the whiteboard cannot draw in a visible colour from its own palette, cannot be used on touch devices, ignores devicePixelRatio, and fakes collaboration with random strokes. It duplicates interactive/GlassWhiteboard. Merge into one pointer-events whiteboard with a controlled strokes API and real colour tokens, or drop the category entirely.

name: GlassSocialFeed
target: dashboard/GlassActivityFeed + a GlassCard 'post' recipe
justification: This is an app-level widget (a Twitter-clone feed) rather than a design-system component, and it has functional bugs: a dead sort control, double-counted likes, a frozen posts prop, invisible content under reduced motion, a full remount every render, and per-card backdrop-filter. Deprecate it in favour of a feed-list/card recipe built on the core list and card primitives.

name: GlassVoiceWaveform
target: GlassAudioLevel/GlassWaveform primitive fed by a real level/AnalyserNode prop + a participant-row recipe
justification: A level meter or waveform is a legitimate media primitive, and this file's button semantics are the best in the social folder. However, the data is entirely synthetic, it renders hundreds of framer-motion nodes, it mutates state during render, and it overrides its own material with hard-coded rgba. Redesign it as a small controlled waveform/level component that takes real audio levels (or an AnalyserNode), drawn on canvas or SVG, and drop the simulation.

name: SpatialComputingEngine
justification: This is a self-admitted mock exported from the package root. It crashes SSR via window access in render, re-renders at 60fps by default through a no-op gravity loop (the only story sets enablePhysics={false}, which hides this), requests an XR session on mount without user activation, and misuses the WebXR API. It contributes nothing to a glass design system. Remove it from the public API and from the certification set.

name: SpeedDial (+ GlassSpeedDial)
target: Merge GlassFab as the trigger; export GlassSpeedDial
justification: This is structurally the healthiest component in the shard: token-driven CSS modules, real reduced-motion support, a controlled/uncontrolled API and a forwardRef. It needs targeted fixes, not a rewrite. Fix it by chaining child onClick, applying the menu/menuitem pattern with focus management, making closed actions inert or tabIndex -1, requiring an accessible name, removing junk position keys, and exporting the glass variant. It should share its trigger with GlassFab.

name: SpeedDialAction
target: SpeedDial (compound subcomponent SpeedDial.Action)
justification: Solid token usage, but it should be a real <button role=menuitem> that is inert when closed, at least 44px on touch, with its tooltip wired via the shared Tooltip primitive and dead props removed. Keep it as a compound subcomponent of SpeedDial rather than an independent root export.

name: SpeedDialIcon
target: SpeedDial (internal subcomponent, not a root export)
justification: A fine tiny internal piece, but it does not deserve a root export, its own certification target and separate stories. Make it SpeedDial.Icon or an internal detail, and use the package icon set instead of inline SVGs.

name: AuraGlassClientBoundary
target: Move to ./ssr subpath; fix hydration logic; add SSR test
justification: A ClientOnly boundary is useful for a library with many browser-only components. However, this implementation triggers exactly the hydration mismatch it exists to prevent, because it initialises from isBrowser() instead of false, and nothing tests it under renderToString plus hydrateRoot. It is a small fix with high value. Fix it, add an SSR test, and export it from ./ssr.

name: GlassConnectionStatus
target: Export from root (or ./app-shell) after replacing Tailwind classes with glass- tokens
justification: The behaviour is real and useful (online, offline and slow detection with a live region), but the styling depends on unprefixed Tailwind utilities the package does not ship, so positioning and icon sizing silently break outside Storybook. It is also not exported from root, so consumers cannot reach it, and it has only one story. Swap to glass- utilities and tokens, clear the timer, export it, and add offline/slow stories.

name: DimensionalGlass
target: GlassCard / OptimizedGlass elevation+depth props
justification: This is a thin wrapper over OptimizedGlass. Its distinguishing props (tilt, depth, padding, zIndex) are either unimplemented or emitted as dynamic utility classes that never resolve. Real depth should come from the material's elevation/depth tokens on one canonical surface. Keep a deprecated alias that maps elevation and depth to GlassCard.

name: FrostedGlass
target: OptimizedGlass/GlassSurface material='frosted' (texture as a material token)
justification: This is the most coherent of the surfaces wrappers: tokenized colors, reduced-motion-aware parallax, and contrast-conscious overlay opacity. It is still a separate component for something that should be a material preset (frost texture plus specular) on the canonical surface. Fold the noise and specular layers into the material engine as an opt-in texture, then delete the wrapper and its five-way copy-pasted mapping code.

name: GlassDepthLayer (+ GlassDepthScene, LayeredGlassStack, useDepthAnimation, DEFAULT_DEPTH_CONFIGS: non-root internals)
target: OptimizedGlass elevation/depth tokens
justification: The depth table is not wired to the material: every layer renders identical level2 glass. Reduced motion is computed and ignored, the 3D transforms have no perspective context, and imperative style writes conflict with framer-motion. Depth belongs in the elevation token scale of the canonical material, not in a parallel layer enum.

name: HeatGlass
target: optional aura-glass/fx entry (decorative effects), not core
justification: This is a novelty effect. It distorts its own content, ships duplicate SVG ids per instance, has a hydration-unsafe Math.random, and depends on animation CSS that does not exist. Its only story is an empty generated box that certification nonetheless passed. It has no place in a premium core surface set.

name: PageGlassContainer
target: GlassContainer / app-shell page surface
justification: Page-level glass is an app-shell concern that already has GlassContainer and the app-shell subpath. The unique features are harmful (whole-page opacity fade on scroll, setState per scroll) or inert (dimensionalChildren).

name: WidgetGlass
target: GlassCard (variant/elevation) + GlassMetricCard
justification: This is a card with off-system colors (blue ring, gray rgba), stacked shadows on top of the material's own elevation, and three redundant entrance animations. It adds nothing a canonical GlassCard with elevation and interactive variants should not already cover.

name: GlassDashboard
target: single workspace/dashboard template using real chart components and a real layout model
justification: A dashboard template is a legitimate flagship surface, but this one fakes its core features: position-based drag-and-drop never affects layout, the chart tile is a placeholder, and the configure action does nothing. Rebuild it on GlassGrid with explicit grid-area placement, keyboard reordering, real chart widgets, and a single dashboard family shared with src/components/dashboard.

name: ChartWidget
target: GlassChartWidget + charts/ package
justification: This is an unexported hand-rolled SVG chart that duplicates the root-exported GlassChartWidget and the charts module. It has distorted rendering (preserveAspectRatio none), aliased chart types, duplicate labels, and no chart accessibility.

name: MetricWidget
target: GlassMetricCard (single KPI/metric card)
justification: This is the fifth or sixth metric card in the library. It is unexported, uses emoji trend glyphs, and shows a broken 0% target bar in its own story. Merge its variant set into one canonical metric card.

name: TableWidget
target: data-display/GlassDataTable (compact/density variant)
justification: This is a third table implementation. It has keyboard-inaccessible sorting and a dead 'View All' button. A dense or compact mode of the canonical data table covers it.

name: GlassDetailView
justification: The structure is a reasonable record-detail template (header, status, sections, tabs, sidebar). It needs the library's real GlassTabs, accessible disclosure sections, controlled activeTab, URL sanitization for link fields, an icon set instead of emoji, and a fix for the style-override bug. The story must show real layouts.

name: GlassFormTemplate
target: GlassWizardTemplate (multi-step) + GlassFormBuilder (single-step)
justification: Its multi-step mode re-implements GlassWizardTemplate with a worse step indicator, and its single-step mode is just GlassFormBuilder in a card. The certified story renders an empty form. Collapse it into a single form template with one stepper.

name: GlassFormWizardSteps
target: single GlassStepper (navigation)
justification: This is at least the fifth stepper in the codebase. It has inaccessible div steps, a length bug in the vertical layout, an ignored prop, and a certified story that literally prints 'Step NaN of 0'.

name: GlassWizardTemplate
target: canonical forms wizard (merge GlassWizard + GlassFormTemplate multiStep)
justification: This is the best of the three wizard implementations: real validation flow, skip support, auto-save and a sidebar layout. It is the right base for a single wizard. It needs controlled/uncontrolled step state, guards for empty steps, focus management on step change, the canonical stepper, and shipped token classes instead of raw Tailwind.

name: GlassDataTable (templates/interactive)
target: data-display/GlassDataTable
justification: This is an unexported, same-named duplicate of the root GlassDataTable, with a 5-page pagination cap, an unlabeled search input, and inaccessible sorting. It only creates name confusion in Storybook and the inventory.

name: GlassListView
target: collection/list template over canonical DataTable + Toolbar + SegmentedControl
justification: A list or collection template is a high-value pattern, but this one has dead filter types, emoji chrome, material overrides, unlabeled controls, and an empty certified story. Rebuild it as a thin composition of the canonical table, toolbar, search and segmented control with complete filter controls.

name: PersonaPicker
justification: This is the cleanest code in the shard: semantic buttons, token CSS, and real reduced-motion support. As a picker it fails its job, because the swatches show no persona colors. It also needs a visible focus ring, theme-aware text tokens instead of hard-coded black, correct list semantics (or radiogroup), forwardRef/style, a test, and a certification target.

name: ToggleButton (+ GlassToggleButton: module export only, not in root)
target: GlassButton pressed/toggle variant (aria-pressed) built on the canonical button
justification: A toggle button is about 40 lines on top of a good button. This one drags in 6k lines of pseudo-AI modules, violates the rules of hooks, records interactions unconditionally, uses unshipped Tailwind palette classes, and contains inert 'eye tracking'. Storybook already files it under Legacy. Replace it with a pressed variant of the canonical GlassButton.

name: ToggleButtonGroup (+ GlassToggleButtonGroup: module export only, not in root)
target: LiquidGlassSegmentedControl / GlassSegmentedControl (single+multi select) with roving focus
justification: The group's state logic is fine. Visually and semantically it overlaps the segmented controls, which are the premium pattern for this use case. Move the multi-select capability into the segmented control (with roving focus and radiogroup or toolbar semantics) and retire this legacy MUI-style pair.

name: TreeItem (+ GlassTreeItem)
target: data-display/GlassTreeView
justification: This item has several defects: focus lands on a role-less div, hidden children remain tabbable, nested expansion clips because of the fixed measured height, the label is forced to black with !important, and a dead spring config is computed. It is not worth polishing in isolation. Fold the compound child API into the canonical tree.

name: TreeView (+ GlassTreeView alias)
target: data-display/GlassTreeView (single canonical Tree with full WAI-ARIA keyboard model)
justification: This is the second of three tree implementations, and the root export already ships a different GlassTreeView under the same name. The color prop is dead code, the items prop is ignored, keyboard support stops at Left/Right/Enter, and the material is bespoke CSS rather than the shared glass primitive. Pixel analysis of the certification screenshot shows a small, achromatic list on a white canvas with no visible depth or intent color. Merge the compound API (TreeView/TreeItem children) into the canonical tree, add roving focus, then delete this folder.

name: GlassPanel
target: Glass/OptimizedGlass surface primitive (expose padding prop there) or canonical GlassCard
justification: This is a thin, correct wrapper around the shared primitive, which makes it one of the healthier files in this shard. Its whole value-add is a padding prop and an error-to-danger rename. Fold padding into the primitive and alias GlassPanel to it. The story masks the material by painting the panel 86% opaque white, so the certification screenshot does not show glass at all.

name: GlassAccordionUI
target: data-display/GlassAccordion
justification: This is a 17-line alias that also drops ref forwarding. It inflates the component count and the public API surface with no behavior. Keep a deprecated re-export for one minor version if needed, then delete it.

name: GlassCheckboxUI
target: input/GlassCheckbox
justification: This is a pure naming alias. The root already exports GlassCheckbox, so this adds API noise only.

name: FocusIndicator
target: interactive/GlassFocusRing + global .glass-focus focus-visible token
justification: This is a non-functional component. The spring targets are never applied, so the ring is permanently 0px. The certification run reported 'no issues', which shows the certification does not check behavior. Pixel analysis of the screenshot finds no ring pixels and no chroma anywhere. There are already two other focus-ring implementations. Delete this one and standardize focus on a single token-driven focus-visible ring.

name: RippleButton
target: GlassButton (feedback='ripple' option)
justification: Ripple is a press-feedback option, not a component. GlassButton already contains ripple code, and wrapping it here double-stacks glass and splits prop passthrough. Move a pointer-event-based ripple into GlassButton behind a prop and delete this wrapper.

name: StateIndicator
target: data-state attributes + tokenized state layers on the base surface primitive
justification: Painting an overlay with blend modes over arbitrary children is not how a premium system expresses state. State layers belong in each component's token set, keyed by data-state. Half of the declared states render nothing, and there is no assistive-tech exposure.

name: VisualFeedback
target: motion preset tokens (src/animations) applied via a shared Motion primitive
justification: This is a grab-bag effect wrapper that duplicates motion presets and ripple code elsewhere. Its feedback props (message/type/position) are unimplemented. A premium system exposes named motion tokens, not an infinite-shake div.

name: GlassAdvancedDataViz
target: charts/GlassChart (single chart system)
justification: This is a fourth chart implementation with a broken legend toggle, half of its declared chart types missing, grid lines drawn on top of the data, and no accessible data alternative. Pixel analysis of the certification screenshot shows a single pale grey line inside a light frame with 0% chromatic pixels, so the hex and token palette does not even resolve to color in the certified run. Fold any useful drill-down/filter/export logic into the canonical chart and delete this file.

name: VoiceGlassControl (+ VoiceGlassDemo alias, GlassVoiceCommands)
target: move to examples/ (non-published) or rebuild on interactive/GlassVoiceInput with a real recognition adapter
justification: This is a mock dressed as a product feature. Recognition is never wired, state setters are never called, and the brand-specific wake word ships in a public library. It is root-exported under two names. Its a11y gaps (unlabeled icon toggle, non-dialog modals) would fail review. Remove it from the published surface.

name: GlassChartsDemo (+ GlassDefs, chartGlass, axisTokens internals)
target: docs/storybook example for charts/GlassChart
justification: This is a static marketing illustration published as a root component. The fixed three-column grid does not collapse on mobile, and the colors are hex literals. Recharts helpers copied from another app (GlassDefs/chartGlass) belong in the chart system's theme layer, if anywhere.

name: GlassLinkButton
target: GlassButton asChild (or GlassButton href)
justification: GlassButton already supports asChild, so a separate link button with its own Tailwind-only styling fragments the button family and breaks for non-Tailwind consumers. Replace it with <GlassButton asChild><a/></GlassButton> and remove this file.

name: GlassPrismComparison
target: AuraOne marketing site repo
justification: This is a product landing-page section with unverifiable regulatory and performance claims embedded as constants. It does not belong in a design-system package. It is mouse-only, auto-rotating, and hides the cursor. If a 'prism reveal' material effect is wanted, build it as a WipeSlider variant over the real Liquid Glass primitive.

name: GlassWipeSlider (+ ComparisonImage, ComparisonContent, FeatureComparison, MetricsComparison, SLIDER_PRESETS, AURAONE_COMPARISON_EXAMPLES)
target: media/GlassCompareSlider (controlled value/onValueChange, forwardRef, pointer events, shared LiquidGlass handle)
justification: This is the only real, working before/after slider in the library, with a solid keyboard model, so it is worth keeping as a concept. The implementation needs a rebuild: controlled API, Pointer Events instead of mouse+touch pairs, forwardRef, collapse compact/preview/contained/density into one size prop, remove dead springs and impossible JIT classes, and render the handle and divider with the shared glass primitive. Strip the AuraOne/competitor marketing constants. Pixel analysis of the screenshot shows a near-white field with the faint divider barely distinguishable (min luminance about 233 in the downsample), so it does not currently read as a premium material.

name: GlassWipeSliderExamples (+ AuraOneVsScaleAIComparison, VerticalFeatureComparison, PerformanceMetricsComparison, ImageBeforeAfterComparison, PresetPositionDemo, GlassWipeSliderShowcase)
target: GlassWipeSlider stories (neutral content)
justification: This is showcase/marketing content with fabricated customer metrics and competitor naming, living in src/. It is not root-exported but is still compiled and storied. Move any neutral examples into stories and delete it.

name: MotionAwareGlass (+ MotionAwareGlassCard/Button/Input, useMotionAwareGlassStyles)
target: Glass primitive + motion preset prop (reduced motion handled centrally)
justification: Motion preference should be a property of the primitive and the motion tokens, not a parallel family of surfaces, buttons and inputs. This file builds fake buttons and inputs from divs, relies on Tailwind classes that are not part of the token system, and emits SR noise in every instance.

name: Icon set (components.tsx: ~160 glyphs, ~220 exports, GlassIcon named registry, *Icon aliases)
target: first-party icon set (designed on a grid with optical stroke rules) or adopt lucide as a dependency
justification: Removing the third-party dependency was reasonable and the factory API is fine. The glyphs, however, are rough approximations, several are semantically wrong (Settings, Command), and the aria-hidden-by-default override breaks labeled icons. A premium system needs a deliberately drawn icon family with a gallery story and visual regression. Either commission or draw a real set, or depend on lucide and theme it.

name: createGlassIcon (factory)
justification: This is a small, correct factory and one of the cleaner files in this shard. The one fix needed is labeled-icon semantics (role=img + aria-hidden=false when labeled), plus a test that asserts accessibility-tree exposure.

name: createIcon (re-export shim)
target: src/icons/createGlassIcon.tsx
justification: This is a dead 6-line shim with no importers.

name: DismissableLayer (alias GlassDismissableLayer)
justification: A correct, small headless primitive that should be the single dismissal engine for all overlays. Needs a layer stack (only top-most layer handles Escape/outside), portal-aware 'inside' detection, and adoption by Modal/Popover/Dropdown to remove duplicated logic.

name: FocusTrap (+ useFocusTrap)
target: FocusScope (src/primitives/FocusScope.tsx)
justification: Internal but load-bearing: GlassSelect, GlassPopover, GlassHeader, GlassMobileNav and GlassSearchInterface all depend on it, and its unstable-dependency effect causes focus to jump on every parent re-render. Replace all call sites with FocusScope (trapped, loop, restoreFocus) and delete this file and its placeholder stories.

name: focus/index.ts barrel (KEYS, isFocusable, getFocusableElements, focusNext/Previous, RovingTabindex) [sibling, internal]
target: RovingFocusGroup + FocusScope
justification: Non-exported sibling barrel whose core helper throws on an invalid selector; superseded by RovingFocusGroup and FocusScope. Remove it.

name: ScreenReader family (ScreenReader, ScreenReaderOnly, LiveRegion, announce, useAnnounce, DescribedBy, LabelledBy, LoadingAnnouncement, ValidationAnnouncement)
target: One public a11y module (VisuallyHidden + LiveAnnouncer provider) in components/accessibility; merge GlassScreenReader and a11yEnhancers LiveRegion
justification: Unexported duplicate of announcement utilities that exist in at least two other places, with hydration-unsafe ids, a mis-roled live region and re-announcement loops. Consolidate into one VisuallyHidden + single persistent LiveAnnouncer provider using useId.

name: SkipLinks (+ MainContent, Navigation, SearchLandmark, useSkipLinks)
target: One public GlassSkipLinks in components/accessibility (merge the 3 SkipLinks implementations)
justification: Functionally decent skip links, but there are three separate SkipLinks implementations and this one is not even exported. Pick one, style it with glass tokens, respect reduced motion for scroll, and export it publicly.

name: FocusScope (alias GlassFocusScope)
target: Canonical focus-trap; absorb FocusTrap, a11yEnhancers FocusTrap, useGlassFocus trap
justification: This is the better-designed of the focus primitives (forwardRef, cancelable mount/unmount events, used by GlassMenuPrimitive/DropdownMenu/SelectCompound) and should be the single canonical trap. Fix loop-without-trap hijacking, add a scope stack, then migrate the other trap implementations onto it.

name: GlassAdvanced
target: Canonical LiquidGlass surface primitive
justification: Has the most complete interactive a11y handling of the surface primitives and real layer structure (frost/ink), which is worth harvesting, but it duplicates GlassCore/OptimizedGlass with a third prop vocabulary, double-applies class and inline material, and has auto-generated 2-story docs. Merge its a11y and overlay-layer logic into the canonical surface and retire the name.

name: OptimizedGlassAdvanced
target: Canonical LiquidGlass surface primitive
justification: A prop-explosion surface where most props are no-ops: every blur level maps to one class, all 12 variants share one class, and the inline hard-coded gradient overrides the rest. Its performance claims are contradicted by its own code. Deprecate with a codemod to the canonical surface; migrate the two internal consumers.

name: GlassCore (aliases Glass, GlassBase, GlassPrimitive)
target: Canonical LiquidGlass surface primitive (redesigned LiquidGlassMaterial / OptimizedGlassCore)
justification: The cleanest of the surface primitives in this shard: token-driven via createGlassStyle, small, SSR-safe. But it is one of six overlapping surfaces with four export aliases, hard-coded radius px, and interactive mode without keyboard semantics. Fold it into the single canonical surface as its static/low-tier path and keep only one public name.

name: Label (aliases LabelRoot, Root, GlassLabelPrimitive)
justification: A trivially correct headless label used as the base for GlassLabel. Keep it but drop 'use client', and stop exporting a bare `Label` from the root barrel (keep it under the primitives subpath) to avoid name collisions.

name: LiquidGlassBackdropSampler
justification: Useful render-prop exposure of backdrop sampling, but it decorates itself with a hard-coded shadow and drops all DOM props into hook options. Split DOM props from hook options, remove the visual styling, and document it as a headless utility.

name: LiquidGlassConcentricFrame
justification: A real, valuable design-system primitive (concentric corner radii) with sound math. Remove the baked-in shadow/color, reuse Slot for asChild with ref merging, unify fallback defaults, and give it a proper visual story showing nested radii.

name: LiquidGlassEffectGroup
justification: The concept (group glass shapes so they share sampling and morph together) is exactly what a premium Liquid Glass system needs and is a flagship differentiator, but today it is a context with data attributes and a transition rule. Either implement real shared material (single backdrop layer, SVG/CSS merge within spacing) or rename to what it is.

name: LiquidGlassLayerProvider / LiquidGlassSurfaceLayer
justification: A sensible architectural piece (glass-on-glass depth awareness is a real HIG rule) but its policies are unenforced. Keep, wire allowNestedGlass to actually demote nested surfaces to non-blurred fills, and hoist reduced-motion into a single root provider.

name: LiquidGlassMaterial
target: Single canonical material primitive (merge with OptimizedGlassCore/GlassCore into one LiquidGlass surface with real token-driven background)
justification: This is the name the library sells as its Apple Liquid Glass core, and it is the right place for a flagship primitive, but the implementation contradicts itself: ~250 lines compute intent/tint/contrast/dimming backgrounds that are thrown away by a hard-coded override at L532-540, four public props are dead, interactive mode is mouse-only, and 'IOR' is a saturate() tweak. It must be rebuilt as the one material engine (token background layers, real specular/edge highlight, contrast-guarded text, keyboard-capable interactive mode) with every other surface primitive consolidated onto it. Keep the API surface small and remove the dead props.

name: LiquidGlassScrollEdge
justification: Honest, useful primitive mirroring Apple's scroll edge effect. Needs theme-aware edge materials (tokenized, dark/light), a ResizeObserver, explicit mode prop instead of children sniffing, and a real story with scrollable content.

name: LiquidGlassTransitionProvider / LiquidGlassSource / LiquidGlassDestination (alias LiquidGlassSourceTransition)
justification: Source-anchored morphing sheets/menus are a signature Liquid Glass behavior and a legitimate flagship, but this implementation is a class toggle with an incorrect transform-origin, unused props, and a keyboard-inaccessible default source. Rebuild on FLIP (measure source/destination rects in layout effect, animate transform+radius) with View Transitions API progressive enhancement and a button-based Source.

name: MotionFramer (also Motion / GlassMotion via primitives index)
target: canonical `Motion` primitive (absorb MotionNative and ReducedMotionProvider)
justification: This is the right foundation (framer-motion, small calm presets, reduced-motion-first), and internal components already depend on it, so it should become the one Motion primitive. But mount animations are broken by the reduced=true bootstrap; fix by using framer's own `useReducedMotion`/`MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` and always passing `initial`. Implement or delete `as`/`type`/`direction`, delete the recursive prop sanitizers (fix callers instead), move presets to the shared motion tokens in presets.ts, and give it real stories that show each preset.

name: ReducedMotionProvider
target: MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" inside the library's root provider / MotionPreferenceContext
justification: Unexported, unused, and strictly worse than one line of framer-motion config. One of at least four parallel reduced-motion mechanisms (plus ~149 files doing ad-hoc matchMedia). Remove and fold the behaviour into the single motion preference provider.

name: MotionNative (exported from root as `Motion`)
target: single Motion primitive built on MotionFramer + shared useReducedMotion (src/hooks/useReducedMotion.ts)
justification: A second, hand-rolled motion engine with a fake physics path, a double-applied delay and a mount flash. Worse, src/index.ts:16 exports it as `Motion` while `export * from './primitives'` (src/index.ts:1125) and src/primitives/index.ts:91 export MotionFramer as `Motion` — the explicit root export shadows the star, so `import { Motion } from 'aura-glass'` and `import { Motion } from 'aura-glass/primitives'` resolve to two components with incompatible props, and the root `MotionProps` type (from MotionFramer, primitives/index.ts:83) does not describe the root `Motion`. Internal components (GlassMagneticButton, GlassSelectCompound) import the MotionFramer `Motion`. Delete it and point the root `Motion` at the single framer-based primitive with a deprecation alias.

name: OptimizedGlassCore (root alias OptimizedGlass; also GlassOptimized)
target: single Glass surface primitive (merge OptimizedGlassCore + GlassCore + OptimizedGlassAdvanced + GlassAdvanced; align with LiquidGlassMaterial)
justification: This is the de-facto material workhorse (~180 importers) and its core path — tokens via createGlassStyle — is the right one. But the public API is mostly decoration: more than a dozen props are accepted and ignored, the 'advanced' flags are data attributes pretending to be effects, the radius scale bypasses tokens, and auto-tier detection restyles every surface after hydration. In 5.0 it should be the one Glass surface: intent/elevation/radius/interactive only, properly typed polymorphism (or asChild via Slot), CSS-driven tier via @supports/media queries instead of post-mount JS, and the fake flags removed with a codemod.

name: Portal / GlassPortal
justification: Small, correct, SSR-safe portal. The issue is adoption, not the code: several overlay components call createPortal directly against document.body, skipping the mount gate and any future shared layer/stacking container. Keep, and migrate those callers onto it (and onto a shared z-index layer root).

name: GlassPortal re-export shim
target: src/primitives/portal/index.ts
justification: Pure duplicate barrel that nobody imports; delete.

name: Positioner / GlassPositioner
target: @floating-ui/react-dom (useFloating with flip/shift/size/arrow + autoUpdate) wrapped as the library Positioner
justification: A premium overlay system lives or dies on positioning, and this is a minimal clamp-only implementation with a broken absolute strategy, no flip, no size observation, and per-scroll re-renders. Meanwhile tooltip/popover/select/context-menu each hand-roll their own positioning. Replace the internals with Floating UI behind the same Positioner API and migrate every overlay onto it.

name: GlassPositioner re-export shim
target: src/primitives/positioning/index.ts
justification: Duplicate barrel; delete.

name: GlassRovingFocusGroup re-export shim
target: src/primitives/roving-focus/index.ts
justification: Duplicate barrel; delete.

name: RovingFocusGroup (Root/Item) / GlassRovingFocusGroup
justification: The right primitive to have, and keyboard movement works, but the register/unregister effect keyed on the whole context value likely breaks tab-stop persistence — the defining roving-tabindex behaviour — and the tests don't catch it. Fix by depending on stable callbacks only (split context into a stable dispatch context and a state context), order items by compareDocumentPosition, add controlled state and typeahead, add a tabIndex/Tab-return test, then make every tabs/toolbar/menu/radio-group in the library consume it.

name: Slot / GlassSlot
justification: Compact and correct for the common case, with a real test. Polish for React 19 ref access, add Slottable and a dev warning for invalid children, then standardise every asChild-capable component on it.

name: GlassSlot re-export shim
target: src/primitives/slot/index.ts
justification: Duplicate barrel; delete.

name: GlassCanvasArea
target: GlassWorkspacePanel/GlassCard + GlassEmptyState
justification: Its only distinguishing features rely on undefined utility classes. Fold into a panel variant plus the existing empty-state component.

name: GlassInspectorPanel
target: src/components/navigation/LiquidGlassInspectorPanel
justification: Duplicate of LiquidGlassInspectorPanel with weaker material and semantics; merge into it.

name: GlassTimelineRail
target: canonical GlassTimeline (data-display)
justification: A labelled box that borrows the 'timeline' name; merge into the real timeline component with proper list semantics.

name: GlassWorkflowShell
target: app-shell workspace template (single layout with GlassWorkspace)
justification: A reasonable composition recipe, but it is a template, not a component, and conflicts with GlassWorkspace's layout. Keep one workspace template in app-shell (with i18n-able labels and resizable inspector) and present it in Storybook as a full-page pattern — that could become a real showcase once the material is token-driven.

name: GlassWorkspace
target: src/app-shell (GlassPage + GlassSplitPane + a single Inspector panel)
justification: Thin layout sugar over app-shell with bespoke white-alpha glass and an equal-width auto-fit grid that is not what a productivity workspace needs. Merge into app-shell as one workspace layout with a resizable/collapsible inspector built on the token material, and drop the duplicate layout path.

name: GlassWorkspaceHeader
target: GlassPageHeader (add a `tabs`/`bottom` slot)
justification: Adds one slot to GlassPageHeader; fold it in as a prop.

name: GlassWorkspacePanel
target: GlassCard/GlassPanel with header slot (token material)
justification: Another panel with hand-written glass and broken header overrides; the library already has panel/card surfaces. Merge.

name: GlassWorkspaceTabs / GlassWorkspaceTab
target: src/components/navigation/GlassTabs.tsx (one tabs implementation built on RovingFocusGroup)
justification: A third tabs implementation that advertises a controlled API it does not implement, fails the WAI-ARIA tabs keyboard pattern, references non-existent utility classes for its focus and active states, and leaks props to the DOM. Replace with the canonical GlassTabs.
